articles.title: IND A vs NZ A: Three wickets, then no breakthrough! Matthew Boyle, Dean Foxcroft put New Zealand A on top against India A
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: New Zealand A fought back strongly after a poor start to reach 218 for three at stumps on the second day of the second unofficial Test against
articles.body: NEW DELHI: New Zealand A fought back strongly after a poor start to reach 218 for three at stumps on the second day of the second unofficial Test against India A on Sunday.Matthew Boyle led the recovery with an unbeaten century, while Dean Foxcroft scored a patient half-century. The two batters added 205 runs for the fourth wicket without being separated, helping New Zealand A stay in the contest.Boyle was unbeaten on 107 off 148 balls, hitting 14 fours and a six. Foxcroft was batting on 80 off 180 deliveries, with nine boundaries. New Zealand A were 128 runs behind India A's first-innings total, with seven wickets still in hand.Siraj, Mukesh put New Zealand A under pressureNew Zealand A had a terrible start to their innings and were reduced to 13 for three inside the first eight overs.Mohammed Siraj and Mukesh Kumar picked up the early wickets to put India A in a strong position. Siraj dismissed captain Rhys Mariu for four, with wicketkeeper Dhruv Jurel taking the catch.Mukesh then struck twice in quick succession, removing Curtis Heaphy for four and Tim Robinson for three. New Zealand A were in trouble, but Boyle and Foxcroft refused to let the innings fall apart.The pair showed patience and gradually built their partnership. Boyle played the more attacking role and reached his century, while Foxcroft concentrated on holding one end together. They ensured that India A did not take another wicket before the close of play.Mukesh finished with two wickets for 44 runs in 16 overs, while Siraj took one for 49 in his 16 overs. Washington Sundar (14-1-44-0) and Akash Deep (11-2-35-0) went wicket-less.Jurel completes century as India A make 346Earlier, India A added 55 runs to their overnight score of 291 for seven before being bowled out for 346.Captain Dhruv Jurel, who was unbeaten on 99 at the end of the first day, completed his century. He scored 105 off 171 balls, hitting 11 fours and three sixes.Akash Deep also made a valuable contribution with the bat. He scored 68 off 116 deliveries, including 10 fours and two sixes, as India A's lower order helped the team cross the 300-run mark.Jurel and Akash Deep looked to extend India's strong position, but Brett Randell dismissed the captain for 105 when the score reached 297. This ended an important eighth-wicket partnership.Akash Deep continued to fight before Kristian Clarke sent him back. Mukesh Kumar remained unbeaten on five as India A were bowled out for 346.Fraser Sheat was the best bowler for New Zealand A, taking four wickets for 63 runs in 24 overs. Randell picked up two wickets for 66 runs, while Jarrod McKay also claimed two.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IND vs NZ: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi on the bench again; Shreyas Iyer makes two changes for fifth T20I against New Zealand
articles.summary: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner finally won a toss in the five-match T20I series and elected to bowl first in the fifth and final match against India
articles.body: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner finally won a toss in the five-match T20I series and elected to bowl first in the fifth and final match against India at Seddon Park on Sunday.After losing the toss in the first four matches, Santner got his first win at the coin toss. Both teams made two changes to their playing XIs for the final game.India brought back Bhuvneshwar Kumar and Varun Chakravarthy, leaving out Mayank Yadav and Axar Patel. New Zealand included Blair Tickner in place of Matt Fisher.Teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, however, was once again left out of the playing XI.No place for Vaibhav SooryavanshiVaibhav Sooryavanshi was once again left out of the playing XI. The teenager has featured in only two matches in the series, coming into the side when Ishan Kishan was injured.India have already taken an unassailable 3-1 lead in the five-match series. They won the first three matches to seal the series before New Zealand bounced back with an 87-run victory in the fourth T20I.Both teams will now look to finish the series with a win.Bhuvneshwar, Varun return to India's playing XIIndia captain Shreyas Iyer said the team wanted to bat first and test themselves after chasing in all four previous matches."[On batting first in the final T20I] Yeah, I mean it's a great occasion to come here, especially in this historical ground. And we were looking to bat as well. Absolutely, we wanted to test ourselves batting first, you know, all the four games we chased. So want to have a feel of how the wicket will play in the first innings," Iyer said."[On India's plans after the defeat in Auckland] In Auckland the dimensions were different. Bowlers had a little bit of different plans against certain batsmen. But also credit where it's due. Phillips, he played exceptional knock. But it's important that we go by instincts and see to it that we bowl according to the plan and also what the wicket requires. [On the team changes and Varun's opportunity] We've got two changes. Varun comes in and Bhuvi comes in. Yes, absolutely. He's been waiting for his opportunity and today I feel that even in the huddle, he gave us a beautiful speech. So he's pumped up and he's looking forward for this contest," he said.Bhuvneshwar was dropped for the fourth T20I after failing to make a big impact in his first three matches of the series. Varun returned after missing the one-off T20I against Japan and the Asian Games because of an abdominal side strain suffered during the Afghanistan series.Santner wins first toss of the seriesSantner said he was expecting to lose the toss again but was happy to get the opportunity to bowl first."I just assumed I'd lose the toss. We'll have a bowl. Obviously a new pitch. Might be a little bit of dew later. Have to adapt quickly to the dimensions. If there's a bit of bounce like Eden Park, it will be nice. Obviously, with the bat, we've been good this whole series. Was obviously a bit more in the wicket the other night which was nice for the seamers. One change. Tickner is back," Santner said at the toss.New Zealand made one change, bringing Tickner back into the side in place of Fisher.India vs New Zealand 5th T20I: Playing XIsNew Zealand: Tim Seifert (w), Finn Allen, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Bevon Jacobs, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (c), Nathan Smith, Adam Milne, Jacob Duffy, Blair Tickner.India: Sanju Samson, Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan (w), Shreyas Iyer (c), Tilak Varma, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Naman Dhir, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Arshdeep Singh, Prince Yadav, Varun Chakaravarthy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'All the qualities of leader': Yuvraj Singh backs Abhishek Sharma for India captaincy, inclusion in ODIs
articles.summary: Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh believes Abhishek Sharma has the qualities to become a leader and could captain the national team in the future.
articles.body: Former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh believes Abhishek Sharma has the qualities to become a leader and could captain the national team in the future.Abhishek is yet to captain an IPL side. He was named Sunrisers Hyderabad's vice-captain earlier this year, while Ishan Kishan took charge during the first half of the tournament in the absence of Pat Cummins.Yuvraj, who has mentored Abhishek and shares a close bond with the left-handed batter, pointed to the way he encourages younger players as one of the signs of his leadership qualities. He also believes captaining an IPL team can help a player prepare for the India captaincy.“Well, it’s too early to say whether he has the makings of a captain, but I feel he has all the qualities of a leader. I think he encourages the younger guys in state cricket as well. I love the way he encourages Sooryavanshi, puts his hand on his shoulder and motivates him. I think that’s a good sign of a senior leader, whatever you want to call it," Yuvraj was quoted as saying by Cricbuzz.“If you want to captain India one day, I think it’s important to captain your IPL side. That gives you the kind of confidence you need to lead India. I’m sure time will tell whether he is capable of doing it. If it’s in his destiny, I’m sure he’ll get the opportunity. If not, then so be it. But I’m sure he’ll finish as a great white-ball player, whether he becomes captain or not.”Yuvraj, who was part of India's 2007 T20 World Cup and 2011 ODI World Cup-winning teams, also backed Abhishek's inclusion in the national ODI squad. He said the batter's consistent performances in white-ball cricket should be considered when selectors assess his chances.“Whether he has scored 35, 100 or 31, 100, the point is that he has been performing consistently in white-ball cricket for a very long time. What more he needs to do to get into the ODI squad, I don't know. Maybe he needs to contribute more with his bowling and fielding. But that will only happen if he gets an opportunity to play," he said.Yuvraj acknowledged the competition for places in the Indian team but said Abhishek would need an opportunity to show what he can do in the 50-over format. He also referred to Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's performances as an example of a young player earning his place in the T20 squad.“There are always areas to improve, and I think unless you give a player a chance, where is he going to showcase his talent? I understand that the situation is difficult right now because there is so much competition for places in the squad, along with some big names. But look at Sooryavanshi. He was brilliant and made his own place in the T20 squad. If you feel that Abhishek is performing brilliantly at the moment, then somewhere you have to make a place for him to play 50-over cricket until the World Cup.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: From sharing RCB dressing room to facing him: Jacob Duffy excited about Virat Kohli challenge
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Jacob Duffy is looking forward to facing Virat Kohli in the upcoming ODI series between India and New Zealand.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Jacob Duffy is looking forward to facing Virat Kohli in the upcoming ODI series between India and New Zealand. The New Zealand fast bowler has already had a close look at the Indian batting star, having shared the dressing room with him at Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) during their title-winning IPL campaign earlier this year.Duffy was impressed by Kohli's attitude and work ethic during their time together. He also spoke about how the former India captain made the overseas players feel welcome despite being one of the biggest sporting stars in the country."I got to see him yesterday. He was in the gym, obviously, so running into him there was cool, but he was awesome to me," Duffy said during a media interaction.'It'll be awesome to play against him'Duffy described Kohli as a "religious figure" in India but said the batter remained down-to-earth around his teammates at RCB."For such a religious figure, I guess you almost say, in India - he's obviously a megastar over there - for him to be so down-to-earth and sort of welcome all us overseas guys in RCB was pretty cool, so very appreciative for him for that."It'll be awesome to play against him now that I've sort of shared a changing room with him as well," he added.India and New Zealand will begin their five-match ODI series in Auckland on November 4. For Duffy, the contest will be special as he gets to face a player he has already spent considerable time with during the IPL.'He was always the first batter and I was always the first bowler'Duffy had plenty of opportunities to bowl to Kohli during RCB's practice sessions. He said their regular net sessions helped both players understand each other's game."He's got a great work ethic. I bowled a lot to him in the nets because he was always the first batter and I was always the first bowler. We actually spent a lot of time facing each other in the nets, so that's quite cool. But also from there, he's seen a lot of me now too, so he'll have good preparation."Duffy will also enter the ODI series with some confidence after bouncing back in the fourth T20I. He had conceded plenty of runs in the second and third matches but took four wickets in the fourth game, which New Zealand won by 87 runs.Duffy has an eye on the 2027 ODI World CupThe New Zealand pacer is also looking forward to the challenge of ODI cricket. He believes the 50-over format offers a different test for bowlers compared to T20Is."Personally, I quite like ODI cricket. What I like about it is that up top, you get a little bit of the hard lengths with the swinging ball and stuff like that. Then you get a little bit of the hit and giggle near the end."With the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa approaching, Duffy sees the upcoming series as an important opportunity to strengthen his case for a place in New Zealand's squad."We've also got the World Cup about this time next year in South Africa. That's pretty high on the priority list, I think."Growing up (watching the) 2015 World Cup, 2019 World Cup, those, to me, are the pinnacles of our game. Those are the major events that I grew up watching and strived for and wanted to be there for those."A year out from that, these games play a pretty important roles in that. I guess we're trying to build and push for a case to make that squad," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Amid Vaibhav Sooryavanshi debate, Gautam Gambhir says, 'my job is not to make everyone happy'
articles.summary: India head coach Gautam Gambhir said his responsibility was to make the right decisions for the team rather than please everyone, stressing that players
articles.body: India head coach Gautam Gambhir said his responsibility was to make the right decisions for the team rather than please everyone, stressing that players who have performed consistently deserve a longer run.India have plenty of options on the bench, with teenage batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi still waiting for an opportunity despite his performances. Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma have continued to open the innings and played key roles in India's successful defence of their T20I World Cup title earlier this year."First of all, my job is not to make everyone happy. My job is to take the right decisions, not the popular decisions. And that is what I'm there for," Gambhir told the broadcasters ahead of the fifth T20I against New Zealand on Sunday.He said maintaining a sense of security within the dressing room was important and that players who had delivered over a longer period should be backed."No, it is very easy to take the popular decision. But for me, I think the important thing is to take the right decision and make sure that there is a lot of security inside the dressing room."Because, as you just mentioned, there's a lot of talent. But again, I think guys who have done phenomenally well over a longer period of time obviously deserve a longer rope. And that is exactly how we approach the series."India had already sealed the five-match series against New Zealand by winning the first three games. Asked how he planned to keep the players motivated with the series decided, Gambhir said representing the country should be motivation enough."When you're playing for your country, there is no complacency.""You've obviously got to remember that it's an international game. Everyone knows how few privileged players get the opportunity to represent the country. For me, every game is an opportunity to do something different, to learn something, to evolve."And that is exactly how we approach the game. I think there are no dead rubbers in my philosophy, in my ideology, and exactly the same philosophy applies in the room as well."Gambhir also spoke about the short turnaround between India's previous assignments and the New Zealand tour. The team had played back-to-back home series against Afghanistan and the West Indies, along with the Asian Games, before travelling to New Zealand."It's been a very short turnaround as well. We finished off on the 17th, flew on the 18th. We had one practice session. I've got to give it to the boys, the way they adapted to the conditions."A lot of boys are coming here for the first time. And we all know how dangerous New Zealand is in their own backyard. So again, obviously, the guys adapted really well in the last 40-20s," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ: Arshdeep Singh creates history in 5th T20I, equals Tim Southee's powerplay wickets record
articles.summary: India pacer Arshdeep Singh continued to add to his impressive T20I record, equalling Tim Southee's milestone for the most wickets in the first six overs
articles.body: India pacer Arshdeep Singh continued to add to his impressive T20I record, equalling Tim Southee's milestone for the most wickets in the first six overs of men's T20Is involving Full Member nations.Arshdeep achieved the feat during the fifth and final T20I against New Zealand at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Sunday. The left-arm pacer dismissed opener Finn Allen in the second over of the innings to claim his 65th powerplay wicket in T20I cricket.With the dismissal, Arshdeep moved level with former New Zealand pacer Southee, who also has 65 wickets in the first six overs. However, the Indian quick reached the milestone in just 99 innings, considerably quicker than Southee, who took 119 innings.Allen was dismissed in the 1.3 over when he tried to pull a short-of-length delivery from Arshdeep. The ball bounced extra, took the top edge off Allen's bat, and flew high to midwicket, where Ishan Kishan completed a fine catch.Allen departed for just two runs off three deliveries, handing India an early breakthrough.Most wickets in the first six overs in men's T20Is (Full Member nations):65 – Arshdeep Singh (99 innings)65 – Tim Southee (119 innings)62 – Blessing Muzarabani (95 innings)62 – Richard Ngarava (96 innings)60 – Shaheen Afridi (99 innings)Following Allen's departure, Tim Seifert and Daryl Mitchell took responsibility for rebuilding New Zealand's innings. The duo put together a crucial partnership to steady the hosts after the early setback. Seifert led the counterattack, scoring 41 off 25 deliveries, while Mitchell contributed 14 off eight balls as New Zealand reached 59/1 at the end of the powerplay.The sixth over proved particularly expensive for India, with Bhuvneshwar Kumar conceding 20 runs. Seifert made the most of the over, striking two sixes and a four to put pressure back on the Indian bowling attack.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IND vs NZ 5th T20I: Mitchell Santner surpasses Ish Sodhi to become New Zealand's most-capped player
articles.summary: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner added another milestone to his illustrious international career on Sunday, becoming the most-capped player in the
articles.body: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner added another milestone to his illustrious international career on Sunday, becoming the most-capped player in the country's men's T20I history. The left-arm spinner achieved the landmark during the fifth and final T20I against India at Seddon Park in Hamilton, making his 143rd appearance in the shortest format.Santner surpassed fellow spinner Ish Sodhi, who previously held the record with 142 appearances for the Black Caps. Having made his T20I debut in 2015, the 34-year-old reached the milestone after more than a decade of representing New Zealand in international cricket.Santner surpasses Ish Sodhi to top New Zealand's T20I appearances listSantner now leads the list of New Zealand's most-capped T20I players, followed by Sodhi with 142 appearances. Former fast bowler Tim Southee occupies the third position with 126 matches, while former opener Martin Guptill is fourth with 122 appearances. Daryl Mitchell completes the top five with 109 T20I appearances.The New Zealand skipper has been a consistent contributor with both bat and ball in the shortest format. Across his 143 T20I appearances, Santner has scored 1,117 runs at an average of 20.30, including a highest score of 77 not out. With the ball, he has picked up 151 wickets at an average of 23.09, with best figures of 4/11.Santner becomes third New Zealand bowler to reach 150 T20I wicketsSantner recently reached another significant milestone, becoming only the third New Zealand bowler to claim 150 wickets in men's T20Is. He achieved the feat during the fourth T20I against India on Friday, returning figures of 2/24 in his four overs. He dismissed Axar Patel and Nitish Kumar Reddy during the contest.However, his record-breaking 143rd appearance did not bring another wicket. Santner went wicketless in his four overs in Hamilton, conceding 39 runs during India's innings.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Glenn Phillips scripts history, breaks Phil Salt's world record in stunning T20I series against India
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Glenn Phillips signed off a remarkable five-match T20I series against India by rewriting the record books, becoming the highest run-scorer in a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Glenn Phillips signed off a remarkable five-match T20I series against India by rewriting the record books, becoming the highest run-scorer in a bilateral series in the format. The New Zealand batter surpassed England's Phil Salt, whose previous record had stood since 2023, during the fifth and final T20I at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Sunday.Phillips went past Salt's tally of 331 runs, scored against the West Indies in 2023, when he reached 332 during his unbeaten innings against India. He eventually finished with 341 runs in the series, establishing a new benchmark for the most runs scored in a bilateral T20I series.The right-hander continued his extraordinary consistency with an unbeaten 65 off 38 balls in the final match, helping New Zealand chase down India's target of 192 with seven wickets and 12 balls to spare.Phillips finished the series with scores of 82 not out, 70, 17, 107 and 65 not out, registering three half-centuries and a century. He also became only the third batter to record four 50-plus scores in a bilateral T20I series, joining Pakistan's Mohammad Rizwan and Japan's S Ravichandran.Four 50+ scores in a bilateral T20I seriesMohd Rizwan vs Eng 2022S Ravichandran (Japan) vs Mongolia 2024G Phillips vs Ind 2026Glenn Phillips surpasses Phil Salt in elite listSalt had held the previous record with 331 runs against the West Indies in 2023. Pakistan's Rizwan occupies the third position with 316 runs against England in 2022, while Estonia's Sahil Chouhan (297 against Cyprus in 2024) and New Zealand's Mark Chapman (290 against Pakistan in 2023) complete the top five.Phillips' consistency was central to New Zealand's batting campaign, with his ability to accelerate against both pace and spin making him a major threat throughout the series.He was named Player of the Series for his outstanding contribution. Speaking after the match, Phillips credited his composure and approach, saying he enjoyed going out to bat with the mindset of being the hunter rather than the prey.He also highlighted the importance of attacking India's spin bowling, particularly Varun Chakravarthy, whose overs presented a crucial phase during the chase.Most runs in a bilateral T20I series341* - G Phillips vs Ind 2026331 - P Salt vs WI 2023316 - Mohd Rizwan vs Eng 2022297 - Sahil Chouhan (Estonia) vs Cyprus 2024290 - M Chapman vs Pak 2023Tim Seifert, Phillips power New Zealand to series-ending winWhile Phillips finished the series with another unbeaten half-century, opener Tim Seifert was the standout performer in the final match, producing a brilliant 93 to put New Zealand firmly in control of the chase.India had posted 191/8 after being asked to bat first by New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner. Ishan Kishan led the recovery with 61 off 32 balls, while Shreyas Iyer contributed 50 off just 23 deliveries.The pair shared a century partnership after India lost early wickets, but Adam Milne's outstanding spell of 4/19 restricted the visitors from making a bigger total.New Zealand lost Finn Allen early in the chase but Seifert steadied the innings and took the attack to the Indian bowlers. He shared a 73-run partnership with Daryl Mitchell before combining with Phillips for an 86-run stand for the third wicket.Seifert eventually fell for 93, but Phillips remained unbeaten to guide New Zealand home in 18 overs.Despite losing the final two matches, India clinched the five-match series 3-2, having won the first three encounters. New Zealand, meanwhile, will take considerable confidence from their strong finish ahead of the upcoming ODI assignments.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Small moments cost us': Mitchell Santner rues missed opportunities after New Zealand's 3-2 series defeat against India
articles.summary: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner believes his side let a potential series victory slip away after failing to capitalise on crucial moments in the
articles.body: New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner believes his side let a potential series victory slip away after failing to capitalise on crucial moments in the opening matches against India. Despite finishing the five-match T20I series with back-to-back victories, the Black Caps fell short 2-3 at home, with Santner admitting that a few missed opportunities could have changed the outcome.New Zealand bounced back strongly after losing two of the first three encounters, winning the final two matches to finish the series on a positive note. Their campaign included a commanding seven-wicket victory in the fifth and final T20I at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Sunday, where Tim Seifert scored 93 and Glenn Phillips remained unbeaten on 65.Reflecting on the series after the final match, Santner felt the contests were much closer than the final scoreline suggested and rued his team's inability to close out the early games."Yeah, I think we'll reflect on that, and we know that it was a very tight series against a very good team. But yeah, I think those small moments, as you said in the first couple of games where, you know, we probably could have won those games or should have. So the series could have looked a lot different," Santner said.Santner highlights positives despite series defeatNew Zealand pushed India hard in the opening two matches. The hosts challenged the visitors to chase a record 226 in the first T20I before coming close to defending 180 in the second encounter.Although India managed to win both contests, Santner was pleased with his team's overall performance, particularly the improvement in batting and bowling as the series progressed."But in terms of a cricketing point of view, there's a lot of good stuff. The batting was really good, and then the bowling - guys adapted brilliantly last couple of games. So, you know, there's a lot of positives. Obviously the scoreline shows 3-2 to India, but could have been the other way around," he added.New Zealand skipper praises bowling adjustments in final T20ISantner also praised his bowlers for adapting to the conditions in Hamilton, where New Zealand restricted India to 191/8 despite a strong partnership between Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer.Adam Milne led the bowling attack with figures of 4/19, while Blair Tickner and Nathan Smith picked up two wickets each. Santner felt the bowlers executed their plans well by mixing up their lengths and variations, particularly after India's middle-order batters began attacking."Yeah, I thought we mixed it up really nicely. I think that was a little bit with the new ball, and then Shreyas and Kishan put their foot on the gas and we, the seamers, kind of mixed it up."Yorkers, wide, a little bit straight with length. So it was, yeah, it was good learning, obviously for us. You know, I guess next time we play at this time of the year is probably the World Cup in a couple of years. So you're learning from these games this time of the year," he said.Santner heaps praise on Glenn Phillips after consistent T20I seriesSantner reserved special praise for Glenn Phillips, who emerged as one of New Zealand's standout performers throughout the series. The right-handed batter finished with 341 runs, including a century and multiple half-centuries, playing a crucial role in keeping the hosts competitive.Phillips continued his impressive run in the final T20I, scoring an unbeaten 65 off 38 deliveries to help New Zealand chase down 192 in 17.4 overs.Santner highlighted Phillips' ability to settle into an innings before shifting gears and taking on the opposition bowling attack."Yeah, I mean, to do it every game is pretty special. He does give himself a little bit of time, and then he can hit some good areas, play some strong shots. And against a good bowling attack, as we've seen."They're a great side. So for him to do it every game and put us in great positions with the bat, as you said at the start, I think the batting's been really good. You know, 200 most games and then obviously a 260 as well. So yeah, and he was a crucial part of that," Santner added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Built as a Team. Won as a Team': Gautam Gambhir's strong message after India clinch New Zealand series
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir underlined the importance of collective effort after India clinched the five-match T20I series against New
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir underlined the importance of collective effort after India clinched the five-match T20I series against New Zealand 3-2, taking to social media to share a short but emphatic message following the team's series triumph.“Built as a Team. Won as a Team. Always for India,” Gambhir wrote on X after India sealed the series despite losing the fifth and final T20I by seven wickets at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Sunday.India had taken an unassailable 3-0 lead by winning the first three matches, but New Zealand fought back to claim the final two encounters. The hosts' victory in Hamilton, however, was not enough to prevent India from securing the series.Gambhir's post came after he had spoken about the team's approach to pressure at the post-series press conference, making it clear that he wanted his players to embrace challenging situations rather than be intimidated by them.'There is no word like dar in my dictionary'"There is no word like “dar” (fear) in my dictionary and directory," Gambhir said, highlighting the mindset he expects from the players.The India head coach also praised the team's response in the opening match, pointing to the difficult circumstances under which they began the series.“The way our boys handled pressure, winning the first game after a 15-hour flight and one practice session was commendable,” he said.India's ability to win that opening encounter and build momentum through the first three matches proved decisive in securing the series, even as New Zealand finished strongly with back-to-back victories.New Zealand finish with a seven-wicket winIn the fifth T20I, India posted 191/8 after recovering from 19/2. Ishan Kishan led the recovery with 61 off 32 balls, while captain Shreyas Iyer contributed 50 off 23 deliveries. Naman Dhir added 33 off 23 balls, and Nitish Kumar Reddy made 22 off 17.Adam Milne was New Zealand's standout bowler, taking four wickets for 19 runs.The hosts chased down the target in 18 overs, winning by seven wickets. Tim Seifert smashed 93 off 50 balls, while Glenn Phillips remained unbeaten on 65 off 38 deliveries. The pair added 86 runs for the third wicket to put New Zealand firmly in control.Despite the defeat in the final match, India walked away with the series 3-2. Gambhir's message captured the approach he wanted to highlight: the achievement belonged to the team as a whole, rather than individual performances.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: There's tension in the Delhi camp. They have mustered just four points in three Ranji Trophy matches.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: There's tension in the Delhi camp. They have mustered just four points in three Ranji Trophy matches. On Monday, an evidently turning track awaits them in their match against Services at the Palam Air Force ground. And their captain Ayush Badoni, with 535 runs in four innings this season, is battling a bout of cold and mild fever.This is the last match of this leg of Ranji Trophy before the red-ball domestic season breaks for the white-ball tournaments over the next two months. Badoni has already emerged as the most dominant batter this season with two double centuries at a strike rate of 90. As he plots his way back into the Indian team's scheme of things, he is also the man carrying the expectations of turning Delhi's red-ball fortunes around.No 26, Badoni's talent from his India U-19 days was never disputed in cricketing circles. He has done enough to stay relevant as an India 'A' player for two years besides showing glimpses of his talent in the IPL. However, the breakout season has come now. Knowing this could be the defining season for his career, Badoni chose to go into solitude and primarily work on his temperament in red-ball cricket after this year's IPL."I play white-ball cricket round the year. I understood I had to work on my temperament to bat long in red-ball cricket. So, I only practiced with the red-ball during the off season after the IPL. Even during the Delhi Premier League, I practiced with the red ball," Badoni told TOI on Sunday.To work on his temperament, he took regular meditation sessions. "I had to find a way to concentrate for a longer period. I had to control my mind. So, I took meditation sessions. My aim is to play for India. I want to play Test cricket and be ready if the selectors need me for the home series. That's why put in extra work on my off-spin," he said."Badoni now knows how to not let his ego get the better of him if the bowlers string a few good overs against. He has learnt that restraint. In the last match in Ranchi, the Jharkhand team were blown away with his innings. They thought 300 was a good score batting first but Badoni got us past 500," Delhi head coach Vijay Dahiya told TOI.Badoni puts in as much work on his bowling as well. He was one of Delhi's highest wicket-takers last season. Delhi head coach Vijay Dahiya would know he is such a critical man for Delhi given the fact that teams are expected to play on result-oriented pitches to ensure their qualification chances.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'That monkey's still on my back': Tim Seifert rues missed century, hails Glenn Phillips' stunning form against India
articles.summary: Tim Seifert came agonisingly close to ending his wait for a maiden international century, falling seven runs short after a blistering 93 in New Zealand's
articles.body: Tim Seifert came agonisingly close to ending his wait for a maiden international century, falling seven runs short after a blistering 93 in New Zealand's seven-wicket victory over India in the fifth and final T20I at Seddon Park on Sunday. But while the opener was disappointed at missing out on the milestone, he was happier that New Zealand finished the series with a win, even if their late revival came too late to prevent India from clinching the series 3-2.Seifert, who had endured a difficult series with four successive single-digit scores, produced a stunning turnaround in the final match, smashing 93 off just 50 deliveries. He was dropped on 13 before making India pay with an aggressive innings that put New Zealand firmly on course to chase down 192 in just 18 overs.However, his hopes of a maiden international hundred ended when he played a back-of-a-length delivery from Nitish Kumar Reddy onto his stumps, leaving him seven short of the landmark.Speaking after the match, Seifert joked that the wait for his first international century continued to weigh on him."No, look, the main thing is to win. But at the same time, you know, that monkey's still on my back for getting my first International 100. So look, you're still a little bit devastated about that. And I think my shoulders and back are getting a bit heavier as well," he joked."But no, I think the main thing is winning. And that's the great thing."But at the end of the day as well, you sometimes got to get over the line, especially because I haven't got one before. So yeah, hopefully it doesn't take another 95 games to get that opportunity. But we'll see what happens," Seifert added.Seifert explains New Zealand's late turnaroundThe opener said adapting to different conditions and learning from mistakes in the earlier matches were crucial to New Zealand's improved performances towards the end of the series."Yeah, look, I think you've got to be true to yourself. You know, you can fall into a bit of T20 cricket. But you know, you still got to be tough on yourself about playing high-quality shots, high-percentage shots for you."Yes, you want to put pressure on the bowlers. But you know, sometimes you can get a bit ahead of yourself and try to go too hard. I think you still got to adapt to the wicket that you play on."So you play in India, you play in New Zealand, two completely different wickets. So no matter where you play in the world, you just got to adapt to what you're playing on. Some will be easier to play shots early; some you might have to wait until the back end of the powerplay."New Zealand had lost the first three matches before registering victories in the final two. Seifert felt the hosts had been competitive in the opening encounters but failed to seize crucial moments."Yeah, I think it was the learning from the previous games. You know, we were close in Christchurch (1st and 2nd T20Is). It's just about winning those little margins when the game is on the line. I think the bowlers, the batters have stepped up and adapted to the wickets that we've played on," he said."Look, that's (winning) your main goal at the start of the series. But when you look back at the series, I think we played good cricket in Christchurch. We just didn't win the final moments."He added: "Walking away from Christchurch, you know, we could have easily been 2-0 up or at least 1-all. So, I think, you know, these last two games especially have just kind of put the nail in the coffin about, you know, those final moments that we didn't quite nail in the first two games."'Take a hat off to him': Seifert on Phillips' record-breaking seriesWhile Seifert provided the fireworks in the final match, Glenn Phillips was the standout performer across the series. The middle-order batter finished with 341 runs, breaking Phil Salt's record of 331 runs for the most runs by a batter in a bilateral T20I series.Phillips' remarkable run included scores of 82 not out, 70, 17, 107 and an unbeaten 65 in the final match. He also became one of only three batters to register four or more half-centuries in a bilateral T20I series.Seifert praised his teammate's consistency and the way he built his innings rather than going after the bowlers from the outset."You know, he's been playing unbelievably in all formats for New Zealand recently. And credit to him. I think for us guys at the top as well, knowing that, you know, we bat all the way down that balance of our team."No matter who's coming in, you know, we just keep on attacking. And look, to break the highest ever in a five-match series, you got to take a hat off to him and say well played. But just the way he went about his innings as well, he didn't necessarily come out all guns blazing at the start, got himself in and then picked up his match-ups throughout the innings. So yeah, credit to him," Seifert said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Bengal, Maharashtra look to strengthen knockout chances
articles.summary: KOLKATA: It’s a top-of-the-table clash and the outcome of the Bengal vs Maharashtra Ranji Trophy match could very well strengthen one side’s chances of a
articles.body: KOLKATA: It’s a top-of-the-table clash and the outcome of the Bengal vs Maharashtra Ranji Trophy match could very well strengthen one side’s chances of a knockout berth from Elite Group ‘C’.Securing a victory ahead of the tournament’s more-than-a-month-long break will place either Bengal (18 points) or Maharashtra (12 points) in a significantly more comfortable position.On current form, Maharashtra must play out of their skins to snap Bengal’s winning streak. Maharashtra’s bowling coach Samad Fallah, who once famously dismantled Bengal in the 2014 Ranji Trophy semi-final by picking up 10 wickets in the match, agreed. “I have told my boys that this is an opportunity to stand up and be noticed against a strong side like Bengal,” he said on Sunday, the eve of the match.The hosts will be back at Eden Gardens for the first time this season after having beaten Delhi in their opening home game at Kalyani. The team has shown resilience in overcoming tough situations to record a hat-trick of wins so far. But coach Laxmi Ratan Shukla is strictly guarding against complacency. “We are in good touch, but there’s still a long way to go,” Shukla cautioned, keeping his players firmly focused on the challenges ahead.Most importantly, in spite of missing two of their star pacers – Akash Deep and Mukesh Kumar, who are doing duty in New Zealand – Bengal have been able to pick up 20 wickets in all their games. Both their pacers and spinners have delivered when needed.However, batting remains a primary concern for the coach. “Yes, I agree our batters need to play better. They are trying their best and I am hopeful that runs will flow from everyone,” Shukla stated.Maharashtra will be eager for skipper Prithvi Shaw to provide a solid platform at the top. “We all know about Prithvi’s class. He’s got a 70 this season and I think a big knock from his blade is just round the corner,” Fallah hoped. However, Ankit Bawne, Harshal Kate and wicketkeeper-batter Saurabh Nawale have all scored heavily for Maharashtra so far.Both camps expect a sporting track which has little grass on it. Bengal will opt for three pacers and two spinners, thereby going for one change from their last game with pacer Suraj Sindhu Jaiswal coming in place of off-spinner Aamir Gani. However, in case Mohammed Kaif, who suffered a head injury in the last game, fails to recover fully, left-arm pacer Geet Puri will get a look-in.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Namibia vs Ireland: Irish have 'learned a lot' as hosts win ODI series 3-2
articles.summary: Ireland captain Lorcan Tucker says his side will have "learned a lot" as Namibia clinch a 3-2 win in the one-day international series in Windhoek.
articles.body:
Ireland 129 (33.1 overs): J Neill 33 (25); JJ Smit 4-20

Namibia 131-5 (21.2 overs): L Steenkamp 46 (44); M Humphreys 2-48

Namibia won by five wickets and win series 3-2

Ireland fell to a five-wicket defeat in the fifth and final one-day international as Namibia claimed a 3-2 series win in Windhoek.

The visitors were all-out for 129 after 33.1 overs with Namibia surpassing that target in 21.2 overs.

With next year's Cricket World Cup qualifier taking place in the southern Africa nation in February, this series was ideal preparation for Gary Wilson's side.

They may not have managed to come away with a victory against the hosts, but captain Lorcan Tucker accepts his side will have "learned a lot" from their experience.

"Obviously, it was a disappointing day for us," he said.

"We came here today excited about the opportunities with the series on the line, but I don't think we quite rocked up from a skills perspective.

"We have learned a lot, but I think we've a lot to reflect on going forward."

Brassell and Smit decimate Ireland's attack

Ireland won the toss and opted to bat, but the tone was set early when they lost Tim Tector for five in the second over.

Andrew Balbirnie was next to fall for nine and while Cade Carmichael began brightly, he became the first of Jack Brassell's three victims as Ireland's innings began to creak.

Harry Tector and Tucker offered some resistance, and while Jordan Neill's 33 off 25 balls spared some blushes, he too was removed by Brassell.

JJ Smit decimated the Ireland batting order with four wickets for just 20 runs as the hosts were set a more than achievable target.

Although Jai Moondra removed Michael van Lingen for 15 in the seventh over, his opening partner Louren Steenkamp reached 44 before being run out by Matthew Humphreys, who took two further wickets of his own.

However, a 30 by Gerhard Erasmus kept Namibia's tally on track and while the skipper was bowled by Humphries, the hosts were able to cross the line with plenty to spare.

"Top-order batting and bowling through the middle period of the innings, I think Namibia gave us a good lesson in terms of how to do those things successfully," Tucker added.

"I think we brought the required intensity, but those skills need to sharpen up a little bit.

"Credit to Namibia, they played diligent cricket and did that for longer periods of time than us - that's why they won the series today."

articles.title: Asa Tribe: Glamorgan batter unable to join England Lions in West Indies amid local Ebola virus fears
articles.summary: Glamorgan's Asa Tribe is barred from joining the England Lions squad in the West Indies because of a recent trip to Kenya.
articles.body:
Glamorgan batter Asa Tribe has been barred from joining the England Lions squad in the West Indies because of a recent trip to Kenya.

Tribe played three one-day matches for Jersey in Nairobi in late October, lining up against Kuwait and Papua New Guinea, as well as against the hosts.

He was then due to join England Lions for a series of T20 and one-day matches against West Indies A.

But concerns over an outbreak of the deadly Ebola virus in Kenya led to Tribe not being admitted to Saint Kitts & Nevis, which is hosting all the games.

"Saint Kitts & Nevis currently have a 21-day non-entry rule in place for non-nationals who have been in Kenya due to the Ebola situation in Kenya and seven other countries in Africa," a spokesperson for the England and Wales Cricket Board told BBC Sport Wales.

"Asa is back in the UK, and we are in touch with the relevant authorities."

England Lions won the first T20 by eight wickets on Sunday after bowling West Indies A out for 98, with Naavya Sharma taking four wickets and Scott Currie three.

Captain Thomas Rew hit 50 not out as the tourists reached 101-2 in just 10.1 overs.

articles.title: 'Most inexperienced bowling attack': Gautam Gambhir flags India's biggest challenge ahead of New Zealand ODIs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has identified the inexperienced bowling attack as the biggest challenge facing the visitors in the upcoming
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has identified the inexperienced bowling attack as the biggest challenge facing the visitors in the upcoming five-match ODI series against New Zealand, beginning November 4. With Jasprit Bumrah and Hardik Pandya unavailable, India will have to depend on a relatively inexperienced group of pacers, led by Mohammed Siraj and Arshdeep Singh.Gambhir believes that if India manage to deliver results in the ODI series, the bowlers should receive much of the credit rather than the more experienced batting unit. The challenge is particularly significant with India having to balance preparations for the white-ball matches and the two-Test series scheduled towards the end of the tour."It's important for me to win every series. It's not just about winning in New Zealand. It's challenging to win every series. Because if you look at it, this will probably be the most inexperienced bowling attack in ODI cricket," Gambhir said on Sunday.The numbers underline his concern. Siraj, with 51 ODIs, is the most experienced pacer in the group. Arshdeep has played 18, while Auqib Nabi and Anshul Kamboj have one ODI each. Gurnoor Brar has featured in nine."No one will talk about it. But if you look at it, Aqib Nabi (1 ODI). Anshul Khamboj, one match. Gurnoor, how many? 10 matches (nine). Only Arshdeep is our most experienced bowler (18)."Despite that, if we do well in the one-day series, the credit will go to this bowling attack. It will go to these boys. We have experience in batting. We have a lot of experience in batting."But when you come overseas, your bowlers win the series, especially in one-day and Test cricket. So if we go ahead and do well in one-day cricket, a lot of credit should be given to these bowlers rather than talking too much about the batters," he added.Gambhir's challenge to Abhishek SharmaGambhir also spoke about the improvement Abhishek Sharma showed against New Zealand off-spinner Michael Bracewell during the five-match T20I series. The India opener had struggled against off-spin earlier in the series but worked on that aspect of his batting during extended net sessions with the head coach, himself a former accomplished player of spin bowling."Obviously, Abhishek has struggled a bit with off-spin. The more he gets better at it, obviously, he will become an overall better player. And you want to keep improving yourself because the opposition keeps studying you."The way you bat, the way you make runs, the speed with which you bat. So if you improve your game, the different areas, if you improve against different bowlers, you will be one step ahead of the opposition."So that's what I was talking about. Because in the first match, when he was bowling off-spin, obviously, he got a little tied up. It was just a very tactical and technical stuff that we spoke about," Gambhir said.Gambhir hails India's 'incredible' T20I series winThe coach also reflected on India's 3-2 T20I series victory, praising the team's ability to overcome limited preparation time and unfamiliar conditions. India had only one training session after arriving in New Zealand before the October 22 opener in Christchurch, but won the first three matches to seal the series. The hosts claimed the final two games."Look, first of all, obviously it's an incredible effort because the boys got only one day to prepare," Gambhir said after the fifth and final T20I."They arrived on the 20th (of October), we practiced on the 21st... different conditions, different weather conditions, different dimensions, playing against a quality side like New Zealand in their own backyard with the amount of experience they had in T20 cricket, plus most of the boys were touring New Zealand for the first time."Boys can be extremely proud of their efforts, especially when you hardly got any time to prepare."Gambhir said the T20I side faced a particularly difficult challenge, with 70-80 per cent of the players visiting New Zealand for the first time. He also pointed out that the ODI and Test players would have more time to prepare for their assignments."If this tour is difficult for anyone, then it's for the T20 side because our Test team will get time to prepare. Our one-day players will get time to prepare. But these players didn't have any time. And 70-80% of these players were coming to New Zealand for the first time."And the weather conditions that we're playing in and the conditions we're playing in, there are two extreme conditions. So, I believe that after a practice session, after a 15-hour flight, if guys can deliver that kind of a performance, especially against a quality side, a lot of credit needs to go to this side."I know a lot of people will not talk about it. But this is an achievement which we should always talk about because these guys were always under pressure and that is what is called ruthlessness. We wanted to win the next two as well, but sometimes things don't go in your favour as well," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Sanju mera first-choice': Ashwin comes to Samson's defence after New Zealand series struggles, delivers witty response
articles.summary: Sanju Samson may have endured a difficult T20I series against New Zealand, but Ravichandran Ashwin was not going to let another round of criticism pass
articles.body: Sanju Samson may have endured a difficult T20I series against New Zealand, but Ravichandran Ashwin was not going to let another round of criticism pass without a cheeky comeback. The former India spinner took a playful swipe at a social media user who questioned his continued backing of the wicketkeeper-batter following another low score in the fifth T20I on Sunday.Samson's struggles continued in the series decider as he was dismissed for just four runs. A social media user then attempted to draw Ashwin into the debate, pointing to the batter's disappointing run and questioning his support for him."Hello Ashwin, your first choice Sanju flopped throughout the entire series @ashwinravi99," the user wrote.Ashwin responded with a witty one-liner that quickly caught attention: "Sanju mera first-choice, tumhara full-time obsession (Sanju is my first choice, he's your full-time obsession)."Samson's lean run sparks selection debateSamson's scores across the five-match series read 67, 14, 18, 4 and 4. After making a promising start with a half-century in the opening T20I, the right-hander struggled to build on it, managing only 40 runs across his final four outings.His inconsistent returns have fuelled debate on social media over whether India should consider giving young Vaibhav Sooryavanshi an extended opportunity at the top of the order.Sooryavanshi featured in two matches during the series, scoring four and 45. His aggressive approach and promising knock have added another dimension to the selection discussion, although the teenager is still at an early stage of his international career.How India fared in the five-match seriesIndia began the series strongly, winning the first three matches to take an unassailable 3-0 lead. New Zealand responded by winning the fourth and fifth T20Is to finish the series on a high, reducing the final margin to 3-2.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 400 and counting: Why India are ahead of the curve in six-hitting
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India hit 289 sixes in 40 T20Is in 2022.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India hit 289 sixes in 40 T20Is in 2022. Four years later, they have smashed 400 in the same number of matches, a staggering 38.4 per cent increase. And the six-hitting spree is far from over. It has merely been put on hold for eight weeks, with Shreyas Iyer's men set to resume their big-hitting exploits against Sri Lanka in a three-match T20I series in December.On the second ball of the 19th over against New Zealand, Naman Dhir's top-edge sailed over fine leg and landed 15 rows back in the stands. It was India's 400th six in 2026, making them the first team to reach this monumental milestone. Of those, 142 have come against New Zealand, the most India have hit against any opposition in a calendar year.India's six-hitting prowess was also one of the reasons behind their 3-2 series win against New Zealand. Indian batters smashed 142 sixes, compared to New Zealand's 61. In pure numbers, that is a difference of 486 runs.A majority of India's six-hitting has come from the designated top three, with Abhishek Sharma leading the way with 86 sixes, followed by Ishan Kishan (60) and Sanju Samson (50). It also tells the story of why India are the only team to have crossed the 100-run mark in the Powerplay twice. India have smashed 145 sixes in the first six overs alone. Across their 40 matches, Indian batters have amassed 2,681 runs in 239 overs, at a blistering strike rate of 189.96 and a staggering run rate of 11.21.These numbers reflect India's dominance in T20I cricket, having won back-to-back T20 World Cup titles. Renowned power-hitting coach Julian Wood believes India's approach to batting is vastly different from that of other teams."I think India are approaching T20 cricket differently from other nations. They're batting differently and not managing risk in the traditional sense. Instead of managing risk, you have to master the skill, and I think Indian batters are doing that very well," Julian Wood, the power-hitting coach, tells TimesofIndia.com."India probably have the largest pool of players playing T20 cricket in the world, which means they're adapting to the evolution of the game quicker. The game has evolved massively and will continue to do so, but India are definitely ahead of the curve at the moment," he adds.Batting has evolved massively, and it continues to evolve very quickly. Batters are now hitting length balls. The only delivery you can't really hit is a yorker.While flatter pitches and smaller boundaries are often cited as reasons behind the surge in six-hitting, Wood believes the evolution of batting has left bowlers with very little margin for error."Batting has evolved massively, and it continues to evolve very quickly. Batters are now hitting length balls. The only delivery you can't really hit is a yorker," he says.Citing Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's ability to hit all around the ground, from mid-off to fine leg, Wood explains that bowlers have little margin for error against such aggressive batters. "If you're going to bowl wide to him, you'd probably have to bowl wide and full. But you have to execute that delivery perfectly. The problem for bowlers is that when they miss, the ball doesn't just go for four; it goes for six. That puts them under tremendous pressure."Wood points to Sooryavanshi's sixes off Jasprit Bumrah and Pat Cummins in the IPL as examples of this changing mindset. "It's almost as if there's a lack of respect, but he knows that if the bowler misses, he can hit him for six. The mindsets of both batters and bowlers have changed. Batters now think, 'If he misses, I'm going to hit him for six.'"I've worked a lot with Liam Livingstone. When he was at his peak, his mindset was similar. He knew that if the bowler executed his skill perfectly, he might get him out. But if the bowler missed, he would hit him for six. That kind of mindset is very dangerous."Sunrisers Hyderabad batting coach Hariesh Jaikumar echoes Wood's sentiments, attributing the evolution of T20 batting primarily to the improvement in batting standards.I think the quality of batting has improved significantly. Players have also started playing fearless cricket. They don't have the inhibitions that batters may have had earlier."You have to give credit to the batters. People say the pitches have become flatter, but even three or four years ago, similar pitches were being prepared," he told this website."I think the quality of batting has improved significantly. Players have also started playing fearless cricket. They don't have the inhibitions that batters may have had earlier. The game itself has evolved completely," he adds.One of the biggest changes in Indian batting since the defeat to England during the 2022 T20 World Cup has been the emphasis on occupying the crease and the shift away from relying on finishers to provide the big hits towards the end. Today, it is the openers who are dominating the Powerplay."I think a new breed of cricketer is emerging. Players who were traditionally finishers are now batting higher up the order. Instead of asking them to face just 10 to 15 balls, teams want them to face more deliveries," explains Wood."When those players move up the order, the batters coming in behind them are also hitters with the mindset to attack from ball one. That's how I see the game evolving. In five years, teams could be full of this type of cricketer. The top eight batters could all be players who just want to smash the ball. We're already beginning to see that," he says.Everybody knows that Test cricket and ODI cricket complement each other, but T20 cricket is now a different beast.Wood believes the evolution of T20 cricket has also had a positive impact on the 50-over format and Test cricket, particularly by encouraging batters to adopt a more aggressive approach."The game is phenomenal. T20 cricket will help 50-over cricket, as we've already seen. Sri Lanka, for instance, chased 430 against India and England. It's great for the game. Everybody knows that Test cricket and ODI cricket complement each other, but T20 cricket is now a different beast," he says.India's 400 sixes are more than just a statistical milestone. They reflect a shift in batting philosophy, where power-hitting is no longer the preserve of finishers but a skill expected across the top order. As Wood points out, the next phase of T20 cricket could see teams packed with batters who attack from ball one. India, meanwhile, are already giving a glimpse of what that future looks like.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Double injury blow! Two key players ruled out as New Zealand name updated ODI squad for India series
articles.summary: New Zealand have suffered two injury setbacks ahead of their ODI series against India, with Mark Chapman and Rachin Ravindra ruled out.
articles.body: New Zealand have suffered two injury setbacks ahead of their ODI series against India, with Mark Chapman and Rachin Ravindra ruled out. Chapman is recovering from a hamstring injury, while Ravindra is still struggling with a shoulder problem. Both players will miss the upcoming ODI series against India.The New Zealand selectors have made changes to the squad, bringing in Henry Nicholls, Matt Fisher, Dean Foxcroft and Tim Seifert.Seifert, who was initially selected only for the fourth and fifth ODIs, will now be available for the entire series. Nicholls will join the squad for the first three matches, while Foxcroft will be part of the team for the final two games.Nicholls earns call-up Nicholls has earned his place after scoring 119 for Canterbury in their second match against Wellington Firebirds. It was his 13th century in List A cricket. Foxcroft will join the New Zealand squad after completing the red-ball series against India A.Matt Fisher, who was originally picked for the fourth and fifth ODIs, will also remain with the squad throughout the series as an additional bowling option.Meanwhile, Matt Henry will join the team on Monday. His availability for the matches will depend on an assessment of his fitness.Chapman and Ravindra need more time to recoverA recent MRI scan showed that Chapman needs another two weeks of rehabilitation before he can return to full fitness. Ravindra's right shoulder also needs more recovery time before he can field at full capacity.New Zealand head coach Rob Walter said the absence of both players was disappointing.“Everyone knows what an asset Mark and Rachin are to this side so it’s a shame they have to miss this series,” said Walter.“I caught up with Mark last week and although he’s disappointed he’s working hard to get back on the field. With Rachin, his shoulder hasn’t quite recovered to a position where he could field comfortably in white-ball cricket, so with the Test series later this month we don’t want to take any undue risks. We’re pleased to bring in Henry who is no stranger to this side, and Dean who recently featured in the ODIs against the West Indies," he said.The New Zealand squad will assemble in Auckland on Monday ahead of the first ODI, which will be played at Eden Park on Wednesday.Updated New Zealand squad for India ODIsODIs 1-3: Mitchell Santner (C), Michael Bracewell, Devon Conway, Jacob Duffy, Matt Henry, Kyle Jamieson, Tom Latham (WK), Daryl Mitchell, Henry Nicholls, Glenn Phillips, Tim Seifert, Nathan Smith, Will Young, Blair Tickner.ODIs 4 and 5: Mitchell Santner (C), Finn Allen, Michael Bracewell, Kristian Clarke, Jacob Duffy, Matt Fisher, Dean Foxcroft, Lockie Ferguson, Mitch Hay (WK), Nick Kelly, Tim Seifert (WK), Blair Tickner, Will Young.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: No longer minnows! Namibia stun Full Member Ireland to script historic ODI series win
articles.summary: Namibia created history on Sunday by winning their first-ever bilateral ODI series against a Full Member nation.
articles.body: Namibia created history on Sunday by winning their first-ever bilateral ODI series against a Full Member nation. They defeated Ireland by five wickets in the fifth and final ODI in Windhoek to seal the five-match series 3-2.The historic victory is a big boost for Namibia ahead of next year's ICC Men's Cricket World Cup, which they will co-host with South Africa and Zimbabwe.Fast bowlers JJ Smith and Jack Brassell played a key role in the win, sharing seven wickets between them to bowl Ireland out for just 129 runs.In reply, opener Louren Steenkamp scored 42 runs, while captain Gerhard Erasmus contributed 30 to guide Namibia to a comfortable five-wicket victory.Smith and Erasmus star in series winErasmus was named Player of the Series after scoring 263 runs and taking four wickets across the five matches.Smith received the Player of the Match award in the final ODI for his impressive bowling performance. He finished with figures of 4/20 in nine overs.Ireland struggled with the bat, with only four players managing to score in double figures.Namibia vs Ireland ODI series resultsODIVenueResult1st ODIWindhoekIreland won by 55 runs2nd ODIWindhoekNamibia won by 31 runs3rd ODIWindhoekNamibia won by 63 runs4th ODIWindhoekIreland won by 130 runs5th ODIWindhoekNamibia won by five wicketsIreland captain disappointed with performanceIreland captain Lorcan Tucker admitted that his team failed to perform at the required level in the series decider."Obviously, it was a disappointing day for us," Tucker said."We came here today excited about the opportunities with the series on the line, but I don't think we quite rocked up from a skills perspective."We have learned a lot, but I think we've a lot to reflect on going forward."Credit to Namibia, they played diligent cricket and did that for longer periods of time than us - that's why they won the series today."Different paths to World Cup QualifierIreland have already secured their place in next year's ICC Men's Cricket World Cup Qualifier because of their position in the ICC Men's ODI Team Rankings.Namibia, meanwhile, are likely to have to qualify through the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup Qualifier Play-off to secure their place in the tournament.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 180 runs, 1 wicket, 4 T20Is! 'Playing Bhuvneshwar Kumar was a mistake': Ex-India star questions selectors
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan has questioned the selectors' decision to bring Bhuvneshwar Kumar back into the T20I team, calling his
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan has questioned the selectors' decision to bring Bhuvneshwar Kumar back into the T20I team, calling his inclusion in the recent series against New Zealand a mistake.Bhuvneshwar returned to India's T20I side after a gap of four years but struggled to make an impact. He managed just one wicket while conceding 180 runs in four matches.India, led by Shreyas Iyer, started the five-match series with three consecutive wins but lost the final two games. Following the series, Pathan questioned the purpose of bringing back the experienced pacer when the next T20 World Cup is still some distance away."In my opinion, where did the selectors go wrong? They made a mistake by playing Bhuvneshwar Kumar in this series. Look, there is no doubt that Bhuvneshwar is a good bowler and a senior player. However, playing him here, when the T20 World Cup is nowhere near, was questionable. If you were preparing Bhuvneshwar for the 50-over World Cup, which is closer, that would have made sense," Irfan said in a video on his YouTube channel.Bhuvneshwar struggles in New Zealand seriesBhuvneshwar's comeback in the first T20I did not go as planned. Playing his first T20I in four years, he went wicketless and conceded 49 runs in four overs at an economy rate of 12.25.He picked up his only wicket of the series in the second T20I, dismissing Daryl Mitchell for six. However, he conceded 50 runs in his four overs.The experienced pacer went wicketless again in the third match, giving away 40 runs. He missed the fourth T20I before returning for the series finale.Bhuvneshwar was unable to make an impact in the final match as well. He conceded 41 runs in four overs without taking a wicket.Pathan says young pacers missed an opportunityPathan believes Bhuvneshwar's selection also meant that young fast bowlers missed out on valuable international experience."By including him in this series, however, you missed out on giving young fast bowlers an opportunity. A youngster could have played in his place and gained valuable experience. Mayank [Yadav] could have played all the matches and gained that exposure, while Prince Yadav could have played too. You missed a valuable opportunity for your fast bowlers to gain good experience on New Zealand soil," he added.Pathan also made it clear that his comments were not based only on Bhuvneshwar's performances in the series. He acknowledged that the senior pacer was also unlucky at times."I'm not saying this because Bhuvneshwar didn't perform well. That's not the case. Although he was a bit unlucky-he bowled well in his first two overs, but later, when he bowled the final over of the powerplay, he conceded runs. These things happen to any player. There is no question about his skill," he noted.'The question is definitely about the timing'Pathan said the selectors should focus on giving young fast bowlers opportunities, especially on pitches where they have little room for mistakes."The question is definitely about the timing. Would this have been a better opportunity for a young fast bowler? I believe it would have been. You have to understand that if you want to develop fast bowlers, it is very important to give them opportunities and let them play on true pitches, where the margin for error is very low," he explained.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Warning bells despite series victory: Seifert, Phillips, Milne expose India's flaws in Hamilton
articles.summary: India may have pocketed the five-match T20I series 3-2, but Sunday's crushing seven-wicket defeat to New Zealand in Hamilton exposed several cracks that
articles.body: India may have pocketed the five-match T20I series 3-2, but Sunday's crushing seven-wicket defeat to New Zealand in Hamilton exposed several cracks that will concern the team management ahead of the ODI leg starting on Nov 4.For the second successive match, India's bowling lacked penetration and their fielding failed to back it up as New Zealand chased down 192 with ease at Seddon Park. Tim Seifert blasted a breathtaking 93 off 50 balls, while Glenn Phillips capped a dream series with an unbeaten 65 off 38 deliveries as the hosts romped home with 12 balls to spare.Earlier, Adam Milne's fiery spell of 4-19 had ensured India were restricted to 191-8 despite half-centuries from Ishan Kishan and captain Shreyas Iyer.The biggest talking point before the match was India's continued reluctance to hand teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi an opportunity despite the game being a dead rubber. Instead, Sanju Samson retained his place and endured another disappointing outing, falling for four. Apart from his 67 in the opening match, Samson failed to make an impact in the series and compounded a poor evening by dropping Phillips on 31.India's innings appeared set for a grandstand finish after Kishan and Iyer launched a counterattack following early setbacks. Abhishek Sharma fell for one while Samson's struggles continued, leaving India under pressure at 18-2.Kishan, returning after missing two matches because of a low-grade adductor strain, looked in sublime touch from the outset. The left-hander hammered 61 off just 32 balls, striking five fours and five sixes. At the other end, Iyer finally rediscovered his rhythm, racing to a 22-ball fifty, his fastest in T20Is. The pair added 93 runs in only 43 balls for the third wicket and powered India to 111-2 after 10 overs. A total in excess of 200 looked possible at that stage.However, New Zealand's bowlers staged an impressive comeback. Blair Tickner dismissed Kishan while Nathan Smith removed Iyer with a well-directed short ball. Milne's pace and bounce troubled the lower order and India managed only 80 runs in the second half of the innings. Naman Dhir's 33 and Nitish Kumar Reddy's 22 provided late impetus, but the visitors ultimately finished short of what would have been a par score.The chase belonged almost entirely to New Zealand. Seifert survived an early reprieve when Naman Dhir dropped him on 13 and made India pay dearly. He added 73 runs with Daryl Mitchell before combining with Phillips in an 86-run stand for the third wicket that effectively ended the contest.Phillips once again showcased why he is among the most destructive T20 batters in the world in the middle order. Fresh from his century in the previous match, he struck eight fours and three sixes and finished the series with a record-breaking 341 runs in five matches.There was one bright spot for India. Kishan's knock took his tally to 1,220 T20I runs in 2026, surpassing Suryakumar Yadav's record for the most runs by an Indian in a calendar year and helping him cross the 2,000-run milestone in T20Is.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India vs New Zealand: Shubman Gill turns up the volume at Eden Park; Virat Kohli opts for gym, Rohit Sharma stays indoors
articles.summary: AUCKLAND: Volume has always been the keyword when it comes to Shubman Gill's preparations for a fixture.
articles.body: AUCKLAND: Volume has always been the keyword when it comes to Shubman Gill's preparations for a fixture. Whether it is the IPL, ODIs or Tests, there is no compromise on the number of deliveries he faces, the sprints he completes or the big hits he unleashes.It was no different on Monday at Eden Park, where the India captain had another marathon net session. It began with gentle throwdowns and culminated in an extended fielding session with spin-bowling coach Sairaj Bahutule. For close to three hours, Gill, who had skipped Sunday's session, made the most of the morning and ensured he reached his desired workload.While fast bowlers Anshul Kamboj, Gurnoor Brar and Auqib Nabi were given a breather after bowling lengthy spells the previous day, a combination of local spinners and fast bowlers worked hard to provide batting practice to Gill and KL Rahul, the only two designated batters to turn up at the nets.The centre wicket remained the focus of most of the action, with Rahul beginning his session by donning the big gloves. The experienced wicketkeeper-batter spent close to 15 minutes collecting throwdowns from Dayanand Garani and Nuwan Seneviratne before padding up to bat alongside Gill.The two batters faced deliveries for close to a minute each before sprinting to the other end to make way for their partner. The drill continued as Bahutule kept a close eye on proceedings from behind the bowler's arm.A handful of spectators had gathered along the main road near the square boundary, repeatedly calling out, "Gill bhai, autograph dedo, main Moga... Punjab se hu." Even Rahul had to contend with the noise as the two batters remained in high demand, with fans eager to get their autographs, selfies and pictures.Once satisfied with his batting output and after putting on a show with his trademark strokes, particularly the big inside-out drive, Rahul disappeared into the tunnel and did not return.For Gill, however, the job was only half done. Having completed the longest batting session of the day, he wrapped up his workout with catching drills from different positions. After working on close-in and slip catching, he also practised taking high catches near the boundary ropes before calling it a day.Following a quick massage to his neck, which has troubled him of late whenever he ramps up his workload, Gill headed off. The ground staff then switched on the sprinklers to give the square some much-needed recovery after the morning's exertions.By the time Gill and company left for the hotel, the remaining members of the ODI squad would have been close to reaching Auckland from Hamilton, the venue of the fifth T20I. The entire squad will have just one opportunity to train together on Tuesday before the five-match series gets underway on November 4.No nets for Kohli; Rohit skips session tooNearly an hour into India's training session, a luxury car emerged from the tunnel leading to the dressing rooms. It proceeded towards the main exit before briefly stopping, allowing the passenger to catch a glimpse of the centre wicket, where Rahul and Gill were batting.Virat Kohli was seated in the front seat. The former India captain had completed a gym session at the venue and left without taking part in any batting or fielding drills.Kohli was not the only senior batter to skip the nets. Rohit Sharma and Ruturaj Gaikwad also chose to stay indoors and are expected to fine-tune their preparations alongside the rest of the squad on the eve of the match.India are scheduled to train in the afternoon on Tuesday, while New Zealand will have a morning session.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
