articles.title: Noor Ahmad's five-wicket haul crushes Zimbabwe as Afghanistan complete  clean sweep in T20Is
articles.summary: Afghanistan completed a 3-0 sweep of Zimbabwe in the T20I series after beating them by seven wickets in the third and final match in Sharjah on Sunday.
articles.body: Afghanistan completed a 3-0 sweep of Zimbabwe in the T20I series after beating them by seven wickets in the third and final match in Sharjah on Sunday. Noor Ahmad led the bowling effort with his maiden five-wicket haul, taking 5/13 in 3.3 overs as Zimbabwe were bowled out for just 79 in under 15 overs.Afghanistan captain Ibrahim Zadran had opted to bowl, hoping to test his team's chasing ability. However, Noor's spell left them with a target of only 80, which they reached in 8.1 overs, with seven wickets to spare.The victory was Afghanistan's second-biggest T20I win in terms of balls remaining.Afghanistan made an early impact after choosing to bowl. Fazalhaq Farooqi and Azmatullah Omarzai dismissed openers Innocent Kaia and Brian Bennett in successive overs, before Abdullah Tarakhail removed Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza to leave the visitors struggling at 13/3 in the fourth over.Ryan Burl tried to steady the innings with 30 runs but was dismissed leg before wicket by Abdollah Ahmadzai. Noor then took charge, picking up five wickets as Zimbabwe's middle and lower order failed to put up a fight. The visitors were bowled out for 79.Afghanistan started the chase at a brisk pace, with Mohammad Akram scoring 14 off five balls before falling to Blessing Muzarabani. Sediqullah Atal added 20 off 14 deliveries but was dismissed by Ernest Masuku, who then removed Noor ul Rahman to give Zimbabwe a brief chance of a comeback.However, Zadran remained unbeaten on 25 while Omarzai scored 18 not out as the pair guided Afghanistan to victory.Afghanistan had already secured the series after winning the first two matches. In the second T20I, Omarzai scored 116 off 50 balls to help his team beat Zimbabwe by 19 runs. Raza's 106 off 56 deliveries was not enough to take Zimbabwe across the line.Rashid Khan had led Afghanistan to a 37-run win in the series opener with an all-round performance.The two teams will now turn their attention to the longer format, with a two-match Test series scheduled to begin on November 5.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Australia have named several new faces in their white-ball squads for the upcoming series against England, with young fast bowler Mahli Beardman and
articles.body: Australia have named several new faces in their white-ball squads for the upcoming series against England, with young fast bowler Mahli Beardman and allrounders Jack Edwards and Liam Scott among those receiving call-ups.Batting prospects Ollie Peake and Jake Fraser-McGurk have also been included, along with wicketkeepers Lachlan Shaw and Sam Harper. Mitchell Marsh will captain both the ODI and T20I teams."These ODI and T20 matches provide several players, many of whom have had opportunities on recent tours, with a great chance to further demonstrate their ability against very strong opposition," said chairman of selectors George Bailey.Beardman, Peake, Edwards, Scott, Nikhil Chaudhary and Joel Davies have made their white-ball debuts in recent times. Shaw and Harper are the only uncapped players in the squads."They are good examples of players who have had an opportunity at the international level and have continued working on their game from what they learnt from those experiences," added Bailey.Australia will play three ODIs against England at home from November 13 to 18, followed by a five-match T20I series. The matches will give the next generation of Australian players an opportunity to make a case for selection ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup, which will be held in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.With a home Test series against New Zealand coming up, fast bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood have been rested from the white-ball squads. The trio featured in Australia's 2-1 Test series defeat in South Africa.Travis Head, Alex Carey, Matt Renshaw, Josh Inglis, Cooper Connolly and Cameron Green have been named in the ODI squad but will not feature in the T20Is.After the New Zealand series, Australia will travel to India for a five-Test series. That will be followed by a 150th anniversary Test against England in Melbourne and an Ashes campaign."We are in the middle of a highly demanding phase of our schedule," said Bailey, referring to Australia's Test players."To manage this workload, each player's build-up to the New Zealand series will be carefully planned and focussed on individual's physical and mental preparation."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND A vs NZ A 2nd unoffical Test: Mukesh Kumar grabs five, Mohammed Siraj takes four but New Zealand A secure 78-run lead vs India A
articles.summary: Mohammed Siraj and Mukesh Kumar shared nine wickets between them, but India A could not prevent New Zealand A from taking a 78-run first-innings lead on
articles.body: Mohammed Siraj and Mukesh Kumar shared nine wickets between them, but India A could not prevent New Zealand A from taking a 78-run first-innings lead on Day 3 of the second unofficial Test at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Sunday.New Zealand A, who were reduced to 338/8, showed tremendous fight from the lower order to reach 424 in their first innings. The last two wickets added 86 runs, putting the hosts in a strong position.Siraj finished with figures of 4/118 from 35 overs, while Mukesh picked up five wickets for 87 runs in 29 overs. It was Mukesh's 12th five-wicket haul in first-class cricket.India A, who had scored 346 in their first innings, reached 32/0 in 11 overs in their second innings at stumps.Yashasvi Jaiswal was unbeaten on 20, while Sai Sudharsan was batting on 11. India A still trail by 46 runs heading into the final day.Siraj removes Boyle, Foxcroft to lead India A fightbackIndia A made a strong start with the ball on Sunday as Siraj removed Matthew Boyle and Dean Foxcroft in the morning session.Boyle, who had scored an unbeaten 107 on Day 2, added just three runs to his overnight score before falling for 110. Devdutt Padikkal took a brilliant diving catch to his left to give Siraj the breakthrough.Siraj then dismissed Foxcroft for 93 with an LBW decision. The New Zealand A batter had faced 226 deliveries and hit nine fours. His dismissal ended another important innings for the hosts.India A continued to make progress and reduced New Zealand A to 291/7 before lunch, with the hosts still trailing by 55 runs.New Zealand A lower order frustrates India AJust when India A looked set to wrap up the innings quickly, the New Zealand A lower order put up a strong fight.Kristian Clarke and Fraser Sheat scored 41 and 40 respectively to take their team closer to India's total. Mukesh dismissed both batters to complete his five-wicket haul.However, the final wicket proved difficult to take. Jayden Lennox and Jarrod McKay stayed at the crease for a long time, adding 55 runs for the last wicket.Their resistance took New Zealand A past India's total and eventually to 424. Lennox remained unbeaten on 24, while McKay made 22. The partnership frustrated the Indian bowlers and helped the hosts take a valuable 78-run lead.Jaiswal, Sudharsan negotiate tricky final spellIndia A's openers showed patience in the final session to ensure there were no setbacks before stumps.Jaiswal and Sudharsan negotiated 11 overs to take the score to 32 without losing a wicket. Jaiswal was batting on 20, while Sudharsan remained unbeaten on 11.Jaiswal also survived a close call in the final over when Brett Randell produced an excellent delivery that moved away after pitching. The New Zealand A players appealed confidently for a caught-behind dismissal, but the umpire turned it down.Brief scores- India A: 346 and 32/0 in 11 overs (Yashasvi Jaiswal 20*, Sai Sudharsan 11*)- New Zealand A: 424 (Matthew Boyle 110, Dean Foxcroft 93, Mukesh Kumar 5/87, Mohammed Siraj 4/118)India A trail by 46 runs.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'We don't play enough T20': Gautam Gambhir asks players to 'stay in shape' after New Zealand series
articles.summary: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has asked his players to maintain their fitness and continue working on their game during a month-long break from T20I
articles.body: India head coach Gautam Gambhir has asked his players to maintain their fitness and continue working on their game during a month-long break from T20I cricket after India completed a 3-2 series win over New Zealand.India won the first three matches to take an unassailable lead in the five-match series, but New Zealand bounced back by winning the final two games at home.Addressing the players in the dressing room after the fifth T20I, Gambhir praised their efforts, pointing to the limited preparation time and the challenge of playing in unfamiliar conditions."You can be extremely proud of the effort that you guys have put in throughout the series. Winning the series, especially when you had just one day to prepare and were playing against a quality team like New Zealand in their own backyard, is a terrific achievement. You should be extremely proud," Gambhir told the players.India also had to deal with a few setbacks during the series. Ishan Kishan missed two matches due to an injury concern, while the bowling attack included relatively inexperienced players Mayank Yadav and Prince Yadav, who were making their first appearances in New Zealand.Gambhir said India had set the tone for the rest of the tour and urged the ODI and Test teams to build on the T20I side's performance."You can go back with your heads held high. We wanted to win the last two games as well, but sometimes these things happen. I thought you guys have set the tone for the rest of the tour. Before the start of the series, I said that you had the responsibility to set the tone. Now, it is up to the ODI and Test teams to continue from where you have left off," he said.India's next T20I assignment will be a three-match home series against Sri Lanka in December. The squad will have roughly a month away from international T20 cricket, but Gambhir asked the players to use the break to stay fit and prepare for the next series."We know that we don't play enough T20 cricket, and we've got a month off now. So, make sure we stay in shape and prepare well for Sri Lanka," he said.The India coach also told the players not to become complacent after the series win and stressed the need to keep improving as a team."We can't take any opposition lightly. We have to continue growing as a team, thinking as a team and playing as a team," Gambhir added.India will now shift their focus to the ODI and Test assignments against New Zealand, while the T20I squad will regroup ahead of the Sri Lanka series in December.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Marnus Labuschagne: Australia batter set to be dropped after 'not taking his opportunity' in South Africa Test series
articles.summary: Marnus Labuschagne hasn't scored a Test century in 49 innings, dating back to the 2023 Ashes; he averaged only 21.83 in Australia's 2-1 series defeat to South Africa; head coach Andrew McDonald: "We believed in Marnus for this tour, we'll have to reassess that as we move forward"
articles.body:
Former Australia captain Ricky Ponting had branded Labuschagne's spot as "untenable" after a lean return at home to Bangladesh left him without a Test century in 43 innings, stretching back to the 2023 Ashes in England.

That has now extended to 49 innings after he signed off the South Africa series, in which he averaged 21.83, with scores of 0 and 4 as Australia lost the series-deciding Test in Cape Town .

"We believed in Marnus for this tour, we'll have to reassess that as we move forward," McDonald said.

"There's still a very good cricketer ‌there. Every time he drops back to state level, he outperforms the others. But he hasn't taken his opportunity on this tour."

Australia have faced some fierce criticism for the way they lost the series in South Africa, with an innings defeat in the second Test followed by a 176-run drubbing in the third - the Proteas knocking them off the No 1 spot in the Test rankings as a result.

Set 288 on the final day in Cape Town, Pat Cummins' side were 60-7 by lunch as they were ultimately bowled out for 111 in a timid display, which former opener David Warner branded "disgraceful" and "un-Australian" .

McDonald, though, backed his players, telling reporters: "It's still a very good cricket ​team with a lot of very good players in there.

"Some are legends of the game, or down the path they will be acknowledged as legends of the game. So we've got to ​balance that out with who comes in, what the next decisions are."

He added: "In the emotion of the current situation, my answer would be we've underachieved here.

"I think people put a lot of sort of premium on the key series, and that's ultimately where you are judged. ​We understand that, we realise that."

Australia much-changed for England white-ball series

Australia's defeat at Newlands was their third in five Tests, jeopardising their campaign to reach a third-straight World Test ⁠Championship final next year.

They next host a four-Test series against ⁠New Zealand in December and January, which is followed by a trip to India to play a five-match series. They visit England next summer for the 2027 Ashes.

Before any of that, they host England for three one-day internationals and five T20Is in November and December , with Australia naming a much-changed squad.

Travis Head, Matt Renshaw, Cameron Green, Alex Carey, Josh Inglis ​and Cooper Connolly are the only players from the South Africa Test series that feature in the ODI squad. ‌None will play in the T20s.

Front-line pace bowlers Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Test captain Cummins are being rested. Mitch Marsh will captain both white-ball squads.

The ODI series begins in Perth on ⁠November 13, with further matches in Adelaide and ​Hobart. There will be five T20 clashes in Melbourne, ​Gold Coast, Brisbane, Sydney and Canberra in late November and ​early December.

articles.title: Australia omit Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc for England white-ball series
articles.summary: Australia's star pace trio of Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc will not feature in the upcoming white-ball series against England.
articles.body:
Australia's star pace trio of Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc will not feature in the upcoming white-ball series against England.

The veteran seamers played all three Tests in the recent 2-1 series defeat by South Africa and have been rested for the three-match ODI series that starts in Perth on 13 November.

Cummins and Hazlewood have also been left out for the five-match T20 series that begins on 21 November, while Starc, 36, has already retired from the format.

Fast bowler Mahli Beardman, 21, has been named in both squads and could make his international debut in ODIs, while uncapped wicketkeepers Sam Harper and Lachlan Shaw have been included for the T20s.

Alex Carey, Cooper Connolly, Cameron Green, Travis Head, Josh Inglis and Matt Renshaw, who also played in the South Africa series, are included for the ODIs but do not feature in the T20 squad.

Although Cummins, 33, formally remains the ODI captain, he has only played one 50-over fixture since November 2024 and Mitchell Marsh, his frequent deputy and T20 skipper, will step in again for the longer format.

Seamer Nathan Ellis, a white-ball regular, is only included in the T20 squad after suffering a side strain in the September ODI tour of South Africa and Zimbabwe, while fellow pacer Jack Edwards is named in both squads after making his debut on that trip.

All-rounder Liam Scott, who played one 50-over match against Bangladesh in June, is recalled to the ODI squad, while spinners Nikhil Chaudhary and Joel Davies, who both made their only international T20 appearances on the same tour, are selected for the 20-over fixtures.

Top-order batters Jake Fraser-McGurk and Mitchell Owen are recalled to the T20 squads after not featuring in recent series, while middle-order finisher Tim David is only selected for the shorter format despite recently returning to 50-over domestic cricket after an absence of four years.

ODI and T20 squads: Mitchell Marsh (capt), Xavier Bartlett, Mahli Beardman, Jack Edwards, Spencer Johnson, Adam Zampa

ODI squad only: Alex Carey, Cooper Connolly, Cameron Green, Travis Head, Josh Inglis, Ollie Peake, Matt Renshaw, Liam Scott

T20 squad only: Nikhil Chaudhary, Tim David, Joel Davies, Nathan Ellis, Jake Fraser-McGurk, Sam Harper, Mitchell Owen, Lachlan Shaw

Follow ball-by-ball commentary on BBC Sounds, BBC Radio 5 Sports and the BBC Sport website and app. Live text updates on the website and app.

Following the final England T20 on 2 December, Australia will start a heavy pre-Ashes Test schedule in which Cummins, Starc and Hazlewood, 35, will be expected to feature frequently.

They begin a four-match home Test series against New Zealand on 9 December before travelling for a five-Test series against India that starts on 21 January.

They then face England in a one-off Test at the Melbourne Cricket Ground from 11 March, celebrating 150 years of Test cricket, prior to the Indian Premier League.

Australia could also conceivably reach the World Test Championship final at the Oval on 9 June, shortly before the five-game Ashes series that runs from 18 June to 2 August.

The ODI World Cup in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe will then begin on 7 October, with their veteran pace trio light on matches since they all featured in the 2023 final win in November 2023.

Cummins has played in three ODIs since that match, while Hazlewood and Cummins have respectively featured in 14 and 11 of Australia's 35 games in that period.

They have played just one game together since the World Cup, against Pakistan in Adelaide in November 2024, and all three missed the Champions Trophy in February last year .

Ellis has played in 23 of Australia's 50-over games since the World Cup, while fellow seamers Xavier Bartlett, Spencer Johnson, who feature in both squads to face England, have played in 12 and seven ODIs in their careers.

Joining them are 26-year-old Edwards, who played two ODIs against South Africa, and Beardman, who was first called-up into an Australia squad for a white-ball tour of England in 2024.

Both Edwards and Beardman have appeared in a single T20, against Pakistan in Lahore in January, and the latter was a member of Australia's highly-rated 2024 under-19 World Cup winning squad .

articles.title: Shafali Verma's heroics, Harmanpreet's catch and Deepti's five-for: The night that changed Indian women's cricket forever with ODI World Cup win
articles.summary: India's long wait for a maiden Women's World Cup title ended on November 2, 2025, when Harmanpreet Kaur and her teammates beat South Africa by 52 runs in
articles.body: India's long wait for a maiden Women's World Cup title ended on November 2, 2025, when Harmanpreet Kaur and her teammates beat South Africa by 52 runs in the final at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai. The victory remains a landmark moment for Indian women's cricket and women's sport in India.The win, in front of a packed stadium, brought an end to a campaign that had nearly slipped away after India suffered three consecutive defeats in the league stage, including one against South Africa.There were several reasons why this World Cup meant so much to India. They were playing at home, had emerged as one of the formidable teams in women's cricket and had pushed Australia, the dominant force in the game, harder than anyone else. India had also beaten Australia in the semi-final to book their place in the title clash. After years of coming close, the team finally had a chance to win the trophy.India's triumph was set up by two players who delivered when it mattered most. Shafali Verma, who was not part of the original squad and came in as a replacement ahead of semi-final after Pratika Rawal was ruled out with an ankle injury, scored 87 off 78 balls in the final. Her innings helped India post 298 for 7. She also took two wickets at a crucial stage of South Africa's chase.Deepti Sharma played an equally important role. The off-spinner, who had also improved her batting, scored a half-century at a run-a-ball before taking five wickets. She combined her ability to generate turn with the control needed to restrict South Africa. India eventually won by 52 runs, though the margin did not reflect how closely contested the final was.Both teams had experienced heartbreak in the past, but only one could lift the trophy. South Africa were left disappointed, particularly their captain Laura Wolvaardt, who finished as the tournament's highest run-scorer. After scoring a century in the semi-final, she produced another fine innings in the final. As long as she was at the crease, South Africa remained in contention, given the depth in their batting line-up. Her innings ended when she was dismissed for 101 off 98 balls, miscuing a shot off Deepti into the night sky.Nadine de Klerk, who had helped South Africa beat India in the league stage, kept the chase alive with her hitting. But with 78 runs still needed and only the last two batters left to support her, the task proved too difficult.South Africa had won the toss, which appeared to be an advantage given the dew usually present during evening matches in Navi Mumbai. However, the expected dew did not arrive. Rain had delayed the start by two hours, bringing temperatures down before nightfall and reducing the impact of the conditions on the teams.That left both sides playing on similar terms. India had more batters in form who could rotate the strike against spin without taking unnecessary risks, while their spinners posed a greater threat. As long as the conditions remained free of dew, Deepti and Shree Charani had the advantage on a pitch where the ball tended to stop and turn. Chasing 299 was always going to be difficult for South Africa.ALSO READ: The coaches who made Jemimahs and Kaurs - architects of India’s World Cup winIndia's total was the second-highest in the history of Women's World Cup finals. Yet, considering what had happened in the semi-final at the same venue, when India defeated Australia while chasing 339, and the depth in South Africa's batting, 298 did not appear to be an insurmountable target.The scale of India's achievement became clearer as they began defending the total. With 11 overs remaining, South Africa needed 92 runs with five wickets in hand. Wolvaardt was keeping them in the contest, but her dismissal changed the course of the match. Amanjot Kaur took a brilliant catch in the deep to send the South African captain back, allowing India to take control.South Africa were eventually bowled out for 246 in the 46th over.The final went deep into the night, but when Harmanpreet took the catch at extra cover to dismiss Nadine de Klerk and seal the 52-run victory, the DY Patil Stadium erupted.Pratika Rawal, who was celebrating with the team in a wheelchair after her injury, had a smile. After years of waiting, India had finally won the Women's World Cup.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Virat Kohli has better chance of scoring century than Rohit Sharma: Former India cricketer drops big verdict
articles.summary: Former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara believes Virat Kohli has a better chance than Rohit Sharma of scoring a century in the upcoming ODI series against
articles.body: Former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara believes Virat Kohli has a better chance than Rohit Sharma of scoring a century in the upcoming ODI series against New Zealand.Pujara feels Kohli's position at number three gives him more time to settle in and build an innings. Rohit, meanwhile, usually has the responsibility of giving India an aggressive start during the powerplay, though Pujara believes his role could change in New Zealand conditions.“The way Rohit bats, he has a role of providing good starts in the powerplay. In New Zealand, maybe that role changes, so he could go for a century. But for Virat, the chances are slightly higher because he bats at number three. His game is more about playing the anchor role. So, for a batsman coming in at number three, scoring a century in the ODI format becomes a bit easier," the former India batter said."The opener’s role is also defined, but in New Zealand conditions, that changes a bit. So, I feel Virat has more chances of scoring a hundred in New Zealand than Rohit,” Pujara told JioStar, as quoted by news agency IANS.Pujara also expects the five-match series to be closely contested. He believes New Zealand could have a slight advantage because India will field different combinations in the first three matches and the last two.While Pujara is backing India to do well in the first three games, he expects the team to face a tougher challenge in the remaining fixtures.“Two-all. In the first three matches, one team is playing, and then, in the last two matches, another Indian team is going to play. So, I think New Zealand have a slight advantage because you aren’t playing the same team in all five matches. I’m still backing the Indian team in the first three matches, as I feel they will do well."The last two matches could be a bit of a challenge, but it will be a hard-fought series. articles.title: Highest-ever! Afghanistan make historic leap, overtake Sri Lanka, England and West Indies in ODI rankings
articles.summary: Afghanistan have reached a historic milestone in international cricket, breaking into the top six of the ICC Men's ODI Team Rankings for the first time
articles.body: Afghanistan have reached a historic milestone in international cricket, breaking into the top six of the ICC Men's ODI Team Rankings for the first time and moving ahead of former world champions Sri Lanka, England and the West Indies.The Afghans have climbed to sixth place in the latest rankings, surpassing Sri Lanka to secure their highest-ever position in the 50-over format. It marks another significant chapter in the remarkable rise of a side that made its ODI debut only in 2009 and has steadily established itself among the most competitive teams in international cricket.Their latest achievement is particularly significant given the established cricketing nations they have overtaken. Afghanistan had already moved ahead of Bangladesh, England and the West Indies in the rankings and have now gone past Sri Lanka to break into the top six.From debutants to a force in world cricketAfghanistan's rise has been built on consistent performances and landmark victories against some of the biggest names in the game.Since making their ODI debut in 2009, they have won 96 of their 191 matches, boasting an impressive win-loss ratio of 1.09. Their progress gathered momentum during the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup, where they produced memorable victories over former champions Pakistan and Sri Lanka.They carried that confidence into the shortest format, reaching the semi-finals of the 2024 ICC Men's T20 World Cup for the first time. The campaign further underlined their growing stature, as they demonstrated their ability to compete with the world's leading sides on the biggest stage.Winning momentum fuels historic rankings riseAfghanistan's latest climb has been backed by an impressive run of results in recent months.They began their recent surge with a dominant 4-0 away series victory over Ireland before maintaining an unbeaten record in the tri-series involving Zimbabwe and Bangladesh.Their impressive form has also extended to T20Is. Afghanistan recently completed a 3-0 series whitewash against Zimbabwe, sealing the clean sweep with a convincing seven-wicket victory in the third and final match in Sharjah on Sunday.The Afghans will now turn their attention to the longest format, with a two-match Test series against Zimbabwe next on the schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shaheen Afridi pleads guilty as Pakistan punished after tri-series win; Babar advised to 'go to Australia' amid poor form
articles.summary: Pakistan men's cricket team on Monday were fined five per cent of their match fee for maintaining a slow over-rate during the Final of the Pakistan ODI
articles.body: Pakistan men's cricket team on Monday were fined five per cent of their match fee for maintaining a slow over-rate during the Final of the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series against Sri Lanka in Lahore on Saturday.The hosts were found to be one over short after time allowances were taken into consideration by Match Referee Jeff Crowe."Their breach was in accordance with Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct for Players and Player Support Personnel, which relates to minimum over-rate offences, players are fined five per cent of their match fee for every over their side fails to bowl in the allotted time," the ICC said in a statement.On field umpires Ahsan Raza and Wayne Knights, third umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid, and fourth umpire Rashid Riaz levelled the charge.Pakistan captain Shaheen Shah Afridi pled guilty to the slow over-rate offence and accepted the proposed sanction, the ICC release further said.The fine comes after Pakistan registered a thrilling three-wicket victory over Sri Lanka to lift the tri-series trophy in front of their home crowd. Chasing a huge target of 326, the hosts reached 331 for seven with nine balls remaining, completing the tournament-winning run chase.Fakhar Zaman was the chief architect of Pakistan’s successful pursuit, scoring 127 off 99 deliveries, his 12th ODI century. He received valuable support from Saad Baig, who scored 74 off 75 balls, as the pair rescued the hosts after early dismissals of Maaz Sadaqat (5 off 7) and Babar Azam (0 off 5).With Pakistan needing late impetus after Zaman’s dismissal, Arafat Minhas delivered a decisive contribution, smashing 61 off just 31 deliveries, including four sixes and as many boundaries. His aggressive knock brought the equation within reach before Shaheen sealed the victory with a six.Earlier, Kamindu Mendis had struck 131, while Pavan Rathnayake contributed 77, taking Sri Lanka to 325 for eight. However, their efforts proved insufficient as Pakistan completed the chase to claim the tri-series title.Yousuf advises struggling Babar to 'go to Australia'Meanwhile, former Pakistan captain Mohammad Yousuf on Sunday advised star Pakistan batter Babar Azam to travel to Australia or South Africa and seek specialised help to address the technical flaws in his batting, saying playing first-class cricket alone may not be enough to resolve his prolonged slump.Babar's struggles came into focus again during Pakistan's big run chase against Sri Lanka in the tri-series final on Saturday, as he failed to make a significant contribution despite his team's triumph in the tournament."He should be going to South Africa or Australia and just focusing on working on his batting now. That will help him," Yousuf said in a post on social media on Sunday, as quoted by news agency PTI.Babar, who has scored just one century in the last three years in one-day internationals, will be leading Pakistan in the two Test series against Sri Lanka from 9 November but serious doubts have arisen over his place in the white ball squads.The 32-year-old, who has 20 hundreds in ODIs, has already been dropped from the T20 format and if he is to make Pakistan’s squad for next year’s World Cup he will have to show a big reversal in form and attitude in his batting.He has also opted to play a first-class match for Lahore in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy, which begins on November 3, to prepare for the upcoming Test series.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Ka mau te wehi': Shreyas Iyer's four-word post after India win NZ series leaves fans searching for meaning
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India captain Shreyas Iyer had a message for his team and fans after guiding the side to a 3-2 T20I series victory over New Zealand, but it was
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India captain Shreyas Iyer had a message for his team and fans after guiding the side to a 3-2 T20I series victory over New Zealand, but it was not in English or Hindi. Instead, Iyer chose a four-word Maori expression that left many cricket fans curious about its meaning.Taking to social media after the series concluded on Sunday, Iyer shared a set of photographs from India's campaign, accompanied by the caption "Ka mau te wehi" and a trophy emoji.The unusual phrase quickly caught attention, with fans and cricket followers trying to decipher what the India skipper was attempting to convey through his post.As it turned out, Iyer had picked a popular Maori expression native to New Zealand, the country where India had just completed their international assignment.The phrase, pronounced approximately kah mow teh feh-hee, is an enthusiastic expression of admiration and excitement. It translates to "Awesome!", "That's amazing!" or "Absolutely brilliant!" in everyday usage.What does 'Ka mau te wehi' mean?"Ka mau te wehi" is a Maori kiwaha (colloquial saying or idiom) used to express admiration, amazement or appreciation for something exceptional.While its literal sense is associated with being gripped by awe or wonder, its everyday meaning is closer to saying "Fantastic!", "Outstanding!" or "What a performance!"The word wehi conveys a sense of awe, wonder or an intense emotional reaction. In Maori cultural and performing arts traditions, including kapa haka, it can describe the powerful feeling of being moved or impressed by a performance.Iyer's choice of words was particularly fitting for an Indian side that had managed to secure a series victory on New Zealand soil despite a challenging finish.India had taken an unassailable 3-0 lead by winning the first three matches, but New Zealand fought back with victories in the final two games.What Shreyas Iyer said after India's series winDespite the series triumph, Iyer admitted that India could have performed better, particularly after failing to capitalise on a promising batting platform in the final T20I.Reflecting on the seven-wicket defeat, the India captain pointed to the middle-order collapse after his partnership with Ishan Kishan had provided momentum."It was plausible honestly. We could have been better considering the start we got in the middle overs, the way Ishan and I, we created the momentum. And then from there on we lost back-to-back wickets. And then suddenly pressure on the new batsman," Iyer said during the post-match presentation.He also identified bowling and fielding as areas that needed improvement, describing the tour as a valuable learning experience."I think we still could have been better with our bowling and fielding. We were a bit sloppy. But great learning. I think coming overseas, coming to New Zealand, getting to play on such different occasions, different grounds. Yeah, great learning curve," he added.What Gautam Gambhir said about captain Shreyas IyerIndia head coach Gautam Gambhir was particularly impressed with the way Iyer handled the responsibility of leading a relatively inexperienced bowling attack.Praising the captain despite the defeats in the final two matches, Gambhir highlighted the challenges of taking charge of a successful side while providing opportunities to younger players."So, I thought that Shreyas has done a fabulous job with so much inexperience in the bowling lineup because as a captain, you're only as good as how your bowlers or your batters perform. And especially with an inexperienced attack, I think he's done a phenomenal job," Gambhir said at the post-match press conference.The coach also praised the team's overall effort, considering the limited preparation time after the preceding T20I assignment against the West Indies.India's 3-2 series victory, despite losing the final two matches, offered another positive takeaway for Gambhir, who reiterated that the team's aggressive approach would remain unchanged.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The BCCI on Monday announced a strong 15-member India A squad for the upcoming ACC Men's Rising Stars Asia Cup 2026 in Doha, with explosive
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The BCCI on Monday announced a strong 15-member India A squad for the upcoming ACC Men's Rising Stars Asia Cup 2026 in Doha, with explosive opener Abhishek Sharma and teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi among the prominent names in the lineup.Tilak Varma has been appointed captain, while experienced batter Rajat Patidar will serve as his deputy for the tournament, scheduled to be held in Qatar from November 19 to 29.The squad features several players who were part of India's recent T20I assignment against New Zealand, which the senior side won 3-2.The inclusion of the 15-year-old Sooryavanshi is particularly noteworthy, with the youngster continuing to attract attention for his aggressive batting and rapid rise through the domestic and age-group ranks.Abhishek, Sooryavanshi headline batting firepowerIndia A have assembled a formidable batting group, with Abhishek and Sooryavanshi expected to provide explosive options at the top of the order.Captain Tilak and Patidar add experience and stability to the middle order, while Rinku Singh brings his reputation as a finisher. articles.title: Naman Dhir makes his mark on maiden overseas tour, wins India's Impact Player of the Series medal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Naman Dhir made a memorable start to his international career overseas, earning the Impact Player of the Series medal after playing a key role
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Naman Dhir made a memorable start to his international career overseas, earning the Impact Player of the Series medal after playing a key role in India's 3-2 T20I series victory against New Zealand.The 26-year-old all-rounder was presented with the medal in the dressing room after the fifth and final T20I in Hamilton on Sunday. The BCCI shared a video on social media showing India's strength and conditioning coach Adrian Le Roux handing Dhir the recognition following his impressive performances on his maiden overseas tour."The one who stepped onto the plate and took responsibility for the team. A stellar maiden overseas tour, capped off with the Impact Player of the Series medal for Naman Dhir," the BCCI wrote in a post on X.Dhir was delighted with the recognition, particularly after being part of a team that secured an overseas series triumph."First of all, thank you Adrian for giving me this medal. I really enjoyed it, especially it is quite satisfying that we won the overseas series. It's my first overseas tour and I'm getting this medal," Dhir said after receiving the award.Dhir delivers with the bat in maiden overseas assignmentDhir's contribution with the bat was a significant factor in India's success. He finished the five-match series with 138 runs, consistently providing the team with quick runs in the middle order.He announced his arrival in the opening T20I with an unbeaten 42 off just 15 deliveries, giving India's batting line-up a late boost. He followed it up with 31 off 17 balls in the second match, maintaining his impact with another brisk innings.Although he could not make a substantial contribution in the third T20I, Dhir struck the winning boundary as India secured a 3-0 lead and sealed the series with two matches still to play.He continued his useful run in the fourth game, scoring 28 off 13 deliveries, before signing off with 33 off 23 balls in the final T20I. His ability to accelerate the scoring rate and contribute in pressure situations made him a valuable option in India's middle order.While Dhir bowled only two overs during the series and did not claim a wicket, he also contributed in the field. His performances across departments reflected the role he has been building in India's white-ball setup.India turn focus to ODI series after T20I triumphDhir made his T20I debut against West Indies in Lucknow last month and has quickly made an impression. He has now featured in 10 T20Is and three ODIs for India. An aggressive middle-order batter who can also offer part-time spin, he has strengthened his case for a place in the side's plans across formats.India, meanwhile, ended the T20I series with a 3-2 victory despite losing the final two matches after winning the first three.With the T20I assignment completed, India will now turn their attention to the ODI leg of the tour. articles.title: Ranji Trophy: Railways fight back after lunch to leave Mumbai struggling at 247/6
articles.summary: MUMBAI: When Mumbai's opening combination of Angkrish Raghuvanshi and Divyaansh Sksena negotiated the first session on a pitch that assisted bowlers, it
articles.body: MUMBAI: When Mumbai's opening combination of Angkrish Raghuvanshi and Divyaansh Sksena negotiated the first session on a pitch that assisted bowlers, it appeared the 42-time champions would go on to post a competitive total.However, Railways emerged a transformed side after lunch, with their bowlers consistently hitting the right channels. By stumps, they had reduced Mumbai to 247/6 on Day One of their Group D Ranji Trophy tie at the Brabourne Stadium on Monday.After winning the toss, Railways opted to bowl first in the hope of making early inroads with the pitch having a fair grass cover and the conditions were overcast. But Raghuvanshi, who scored 78 off 122 balls with 11 fours and two sixes, and Sksena, who made 39 off 96 deliveries, curbed their natural instincts and batted cautiously to see off the new ball as Mumbai reached 109 without loss at lunch.The innings break came at the wrong time for Mumbai as Railways claimed three wickets in the first nine overs of the second session to leave them reeling at 128/3. With the sun out, the ball started carrying much better and posed a sterner test for the Mumbai batters.Leading the charge was right-arm pacer Himanshu Singh (3/32), who dismissed Sksena in the very first over after lunch. Three overs later, pacer Adarsh Singh (2/60) induced Musheer Khan (4) to edge one straight to substitute wicketkeeper Suraj Ahuja. Sangwan then had Raghuvanshi caught behind, putting Mumbai under severe pressure.Just when it looked like Railways would tighten their grip further, Siddhesh Lad (47, 125b; 4x4) and Sarfaraz Khan (55, 100b; 7x4) dug in, absorbed the pressure and engineered a recovery. They safely negotiated the remainder of the second session, but just when they seemed to have steadied the innings, both departed within the space of 10 balls in the last session.The pair added 98 runs for the fourth wicket off 205 balls before Lad chopped a Sangwan delivery onto his stumps. Moments later, Adarsh extracted extra bounce and movement from the surface, catching Sarfaraz by surprise and inducing an edge to end his stay at the crease.Mumbai slipped further to 238/6 when Suryansh Shedge, making his first appearance of the season, drove one straight to cover off Mohammad Saif. At stumps, Akash Anand (16*) and Shams Mulani (2*) were unbeaten at the crease.Sarfaraz admitted after play that it was not a typical CCI wicket and that the overcast conditions made batting challenging throughout the day. "The wicket and conditions weren't easy. The ball was moving throughout the day. Tomorrow will be important and we'll look to bat for at least two sessions as we still have good batters to come," said Sarfaraz.Railways pacer Sangwan said the surface was a bit sticky during the opening session, preventing the ball from carrying well. However, once the sun came out and the pitch dried up, the bowlers were able to extract more assistance, which resulted in the three quick wickets at the start of the second session.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Why should I wake up at 5 am?': Sarfaraz Khan opens up on India snubs, motivation and father's support
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The shrug of the shoulder said it all when Sarfaraz Khan was asked about his absence from the India Test set-up.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The shrug of the shoulder said it all when Sarfaraz Khan was asked about his absence from the India Test set-up.The latest snub came when he was overlooked for India A's three-match tour of New Zealand. This was after he had been included in the Test squad for the Sri Lanka tour as Sai Sudharsan's replacement.Quizzed about what keeps him motivated despite repeatedly being overlooked, the 29-year-old said he often finds himself questioning the effort he puts in every day."I wake up every morning and ask myself the same question. Why should I work harder? Why do the same things? Why should I wake up at 5 am (for practice)? I have already played for India. So even with basic effort, I can still play for Mumbai. With that effort, I can still get those 50s and 100s. So sometimes I start questioning it (the effort). But when I see Abbu (father Naushad) putting in that effort, I think of going out there and performing for him. So there is something or the other that keeps motivating me," said the Mumbai batter.Sarfaraz last played for India when New Zealand toured the country in 2024. He was also part of the squad for India's 2024-25 tour of Australia but did not get a game Down Under.He added: "Right now, the motivation is to play cricket. I don't like to sit at home. I think I'm made for cricket. Wherever I get an opportunity... Ranji Trophy, Mushtaq Ali, Vijay Hazare, IPL, or if the Indian team calls me. I just want to play cricket."As far as communication from the national selectors is concerned, Sarfaraz feels let down by the perception that he is only being considered for Indian conditions."The selector didn't say it directly. But when I went with the Indian team, I heard that they are looking at me more for Indian conditions. But I will question that (thinking). I have scored centuries in South Africa and England (during intra-squad matches). In India, you get such big rank turners. You struggle so much when you come from domestic cricket. And suddenly, you will not be able to perform on such a difficult wicket... so you can't get more than 30-40 runs," said Sarfaraz, who made a 100-ball 55 on Day One of Mumbai's Group D match against Railways at the Brabourne Stadium on Monday.The centuries Sarfaraz is referring to came during intra-squad games. In 2023, he scored a 61-ball century in Pretoria, while during the 2025 England tour, he made a 76-ball 101 for India A against the Indian Test squad.Despite the setbacks, he focused on improving his fitness, and skills, in the off-season and shedding a few kilos as well. He has lost 22kg and now tips the scales at 77kg, having once weighed 97kg. Right now, he is looking forward to scoring runs in the domestic season and staying ready for an India call-up so that he is not found wanting.But when it comes to Sarfaraz, a tongue-in-cheek comment is never far away, even if his career is at a crossroads. "I used to play better when I was fat," he said cheekily, before adding: "It is not like I'm not getting runs. You can't get the same amount of runs every year. Sometimes it's up and down. As long as you are not out of form, you don't have to worry. In reality, my weight was more."Sarfaraz still boasts a healthy first-class record, having scored 5,354 runs in 66 matches at an average of 63.73, including 18 centuries.He feels restarting every season isn't easy, nor is scoring truckloads of runs year after year. All he can do is work as hard as possible. "It's very difficult to make runs. My routine, after playing for so many years in the Ranji Trophy, hasn't changed. There's no off-season for me... I just keep practising. I don't know how many runs I am going to make, but the hard work I put in is the same. Everyone knows, if you want to meet Sarfaraz, you don't have to come to his home. You can meet him at Azad or Cross Maidan. It's very difficult to restart. Sometimes you get success, sometimes you don't. But this is the job," said Sarfaraz.One regret Sarfaraz has is not getting enough support in his push for an India spot. "Everyone knows that I don't have support in my life. Only my father has supported me. But it's okay. I have fulfilled my father's dream (of me playing for India). And it's not like I scored once or twice and immediately played for India. I scored 300, 250, 200 and worked hard to get that opportunity," he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ireland Cricket: Rebecca Stokell in 'voluntary suspension' after medication error
articles.summary: Ireland cricketer Rebecca Stokell says she will "fully accept" responsibility for an inadvertent breach of reporting requirements regarding the use of prescription medication and has begun a "voluntary suspension".
articles.body:
Ireland cricketer Rebecca Stokell said she will "fully accept" responsibility for an inadvertent breach of reporting requirements regarding the use of prescription medication and has begun a "voluntary suspension".

The International Cricket Council (ICC) confirmed the 26-year-old was drug tested and "returned an adverse finding for a specified substance" after her side's defeat by Sri Lanka at the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup in June.

Although the substance was not performance-enhancing, Stokell has acknowledged she did not adhere to reporting requirements over the use of prescription medication and has started a voluntary period of suspension while waiting for the outcome of an ICC investigation.

"I fully accept my mistake and have voluntarily entered into a period of suspension ahead of the findings being returned," said Stokell in a statement.

"While this was not performance-related in any way, I understand that I am responsible for following the anti-doping guidelines and I hope that I can be back playing for Ireland as soon as possible."

Graeme West, the director of high performance at Cricket Ireland, added: "While we feel very sorry for Rebecca and have provided the level of support appropriate in these circumstances, this incident does serve as a reminder to all our international players that the anti-doping rules are in place to protect both the sport and the athletes themselves.

"All players must adhere to the standards and responsibilities expected, and we will continue to educate our players regularly on these matters and why they are important."

Stokell made her international debut in 2017 and has featured 109 times for Ireland across all formats.

articles.title: Nine wickets before India A call-up! Harsh Dubey scripts history with stunning Ranji Trophy spell
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Harsh Dubey had a Monday to remember.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Harsh Dubey had a Monday to remember. Hours before being named in India's 15-member squad for the ACC Men's Rising Stars Asia Cup, the left-arm spinner produced a sensational nine-wicket haul to rewrite Vidarbha's record books in the Ranji Trophy.Dubey returned remarkable figures of 9/53 to bowl Madhya Pradesh out for 209 on the opening day of their Elite Group A encounter at the VCA Stadium in Jamtha. He became the first Vidarbha bowler to claim nine wickets in a single innings in the tournament's history and joined an exclusive list of bowlers to have achieved the feat.The 23.1-over spell also made him only the 30th bowler overall to take nine or more wickets in a Ranji Trophy innings.The previous best figures for Vidarbha belonged to Arun Ogiral, who claimed 8/39 against Madhya Pradesh in the 1967-68 season. Nearly six decades later, Dubey bettered that mark against the same opposition.Dubey's record-breaking spell puts MP on the matAfter Madhya Pradesh elected to bat, Nachiket Bhute provided Vidarbha with the first breakthrough by dismissing opener Yash Dubey. From there, the day belonged almost entirely to Harsh Dubey.The left-arm spinner opened his account in the 17th over and kept striking at regular intervals, reducing Madhya Pradesh to 64/5 by the 29th over. Atharva Mahajan offered resistance with a fighting 85 off 123 balls, while Saransh Jain contributed 34.The duo put together a 72-run partnership to briefly revive the innings, but Dubey returned to break the stand and dismantled the lower order. Madhya Pradesh were eventually bowled out for 209 in 66.1 overs, with Dubey claiming nine wickets and Bhute taking the other.The last nine-wicket haul in the Ranji Trophy came from Gujarat's left-arm spinner Siddharth Desai, who registered figures of 9/36 against Uttarakhand in the 2024-25 season.Vidarbha, however, also had a difficult time with the bat, ending the day at 56/4 in 23 overs. Kumar Kartikeya claimed three wickets for Madhya Pradesh, while Avesh Khan picked up one, leaving the hosts trailing by 153 runs.India A selection caps a remarkable yearDubey's record-breaking performance added another milestone to an impressive year. He made his ODI debut against Afghanistan in June, taking four wickets in two matches, before touring Sri Lanka with India A, where he claimed three wickets and scored 59 runs across two innings.He also represented Central Zone in the Duleep Trophy, taking eight wickets and contributing scores of 27 and 24 against East Zone.The 2026-27 Ranji Trophy season has been another productive one for the all-rounder, who has already claimed 23 wickets in seven innings.His latest achievement came just as the BCCI announced India's squad for the Rising Stars Asia Cup, scheduled to be held in Doha from November 19 to 29. Led by Tilak Varma, with Rajat Patidar as vice-captain, the squad also features Abhishek Sharma and teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.Dubey's inclusion adds another reward to a season in which he has continued to strengthen his credentials as one of India's promising spin-bowling all-rounders.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Will PCB issue NOC to Pakistan players for Afghanistan Premier League? List of Pakistan stars who have registered for APL
articles.summary: With 30 Pakistani players registered for the Afganistan Premier League, fans are still not sure if the PCB will issue an NOC to the players.
articles.body:
A PCB spokesperson has indicated that No-Objection Certificates for the Afghanistan Premier League are unlikely.

Twenty-nine Pakistan players have registered for the draft in Dubai on Tuesday.

The Afghanistan Cricket Board's own register makes their availability conditional on PCB clearance.

Will the PCB issue NOCs to Pakistan players for the APL?

Twenty-nine Pakistan cricketers put their names into the Afghanistan Premier League draft, which takes place in Dubai on Tuesday, November 3. On current indications, most of them will not be going anywhere.

Asked by Cricbuzz whether the Pakistan Cricket Board would grant the required No-Objection Certificates, a spokesperson said simply: "I don't think so." There are reports that applications have already been rejected, against a backdrop of diplomatic tension between Pakistan and Afghanistan.

The Afghanistan Cricket Board has acknowledged the problem in its own paperwork. The auction register, which shortlists 462 players in all, formally states that the availability of Pakistan players is subject to NOCs being received from the PCB.

One Pakistan-born name on the list is unaffected. Mohammad Amir has registered as a UK national, with Pakistan listed only as his country of residence, which removes the NOC requirement altogether and places him in the Platinum category.

This is not the first time this year the board has held up clearances. In October, the PCB withheld NOCs for seven Pakistan players signed by Nepal Premier League franchises, reportedly seeking a payment of USD 25,000 per player, the same figure that caused a standoff over Major League Cricket in July.

List of Pakistan players registered for the APL draft

The register includes current T20I regulars alongside several senior names, with the tournament itself due to begin on December 27.

Fakhar Zaman registered days after top-scoring in the ODI tri-series final in Lahore, while Saim Ayub, Hasan Nawaz, Arafat Minhas and Naseem Shah are all part of Pakistan's current white-ball plans.

They are not the only overseas contingent in doubt. Ten Bangladesh players are also on the register, with Mushfiqur Rahim, Mehidy Hasan Miraz, Taskin Ahmed, Mustafizur Rahman and Rishad Hossain in the Platinum bracket and Shakib Al Hasan in Diamond.

The Cricket News Opinion: Why the NOC question matters beyond this draft

For the APL, the stakes are straightforward. It is a five-team league with 6-7 overseas slots per side, and 29 Pakistan registrations represent a significant share of the pool that franchises will be bidding on. Losing them means a thinner tournament in its first properly marketed edition.

For the players, the issue is income. Platinum-category fees are USD 100,000 and team purses run between USD 650,000 and USD 750,000, and for the senior names on that list the franchise circuit is an increasingly large part of what they earn.

The wider pattern is the one worth watching. Between the MLC standoff in July, the Nepal Premier League NOCs in October and now the APL, the PCB has blocked or delayed clearances three times in four months. Amir's registration as a UK national points to where that leads if it continues.

articles.title: India vs Pakistan 2027 World Cup tie has 8.4m applications for tickets
articles.summary: Organisers say 8.4m people have applied for tickets to India v Pakistan at the Men's Cricket World Cup in Johannesburg in 2027.
articles.body:
There have been nearly 8.4 million requests for tickets for the group stage match between India and Pakistan at next year's ICC Men's Cricket World Cup.

The 2027 edition of the tournament is being co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.

The rivals face each other on 10 October at Johannesburg's Wanderers stadium, which holds just 34,000 spectators.

The same venue is also hosting the final on 21 November, which has resulted in almost eight million ticket applications.

The tournament opener on 7 October will be a repeat of the 2023 final which saw Australia stun India in Ahmedabad.

Although India v Pakistan is one of the most highly-anticipated matches in the cricket calendar and the most lucrative financially, it has been a one-sided affair in recent times with India winning their past nine meetings.

Pakistan's last win against India came in the 2022 Asia Cup.

They are in a group with Australia, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and a qualifier while England join South Africa, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, New Zealand and another qualifier.

The top three, plus the best fourth-placed finisher, from the two groups progress to the Super 7 stage and from there, the top four teams will qualify for the semi-finals.

articles.title: Australia's Glenn Maxwell announces retirement from international cricket
articles.summary: Glenn Maxwell had already retired from one-day internationals and has now called time on his T20 international career as well; batting all-rounder's last appearance for his country came at 2026 T20 World Cup; Maxwell hit the fastest 50-over World Cup century, from 40 balls, in 2023
articles.body:
The 38-year-old's final appearance for his country came against Oman in the T20 World Cup earlier this year, when he recorded figures of 2-13 from three overs with his off-spin and was not required to bat.

Maxwell scored five T20 international hundreds, a record he shares with India's Rohit Sharma, while he is one of only five Australian men, alongside Shane Watson, David Warner, Josh Inglis and Mitchell Marsh, to score a ton in all three international formats.

Speaking on the Final Word podcast, Maxwell said: "I suppose [I had] a small hope that I might have been able to potentially get a send-off game at the MCG. But I can completely understand the direction they're going with this [T20] squad.

"There's going to be a lot of change over the next 12 to 24 months with the Olympics coming up [in 2028], and they've got to make sure they get their eyeballs on a few young guys coming through, making sure they're getting exposed to international pressure."

Maxwell - who said he had considered trying to get ready for Australia's T20 series at home to England in late November, which includes a match in Melbourne - quit one-day international cricket in June of last year, the format in which he put in his most memorable performance during the 2023 World Cup.

He plundered a match-winning 201 not out from 128 balls against Afghanistan while battling injury as Australia recovered from 91-7 to reach a target of 292.

Maxwell's 128-ball double hundred was the-then second-fastest in all ODIs, behind India star Ishan Kishan's 126-ball effort versus Bangladesh in 2022, but is now fourth.

England white-ball captain Harry Brook smoked the quickest ODI double ton from 114 balls against Sri Lanka in October, after India's Shubman Gill had done so from 117 deliveries versus West Indies less than a month earlier.

Maxwell's heroics against Afghanistan three years ago came in a tournament in which he also hit the fastest 50-over World Cup century, from 40 deliveries against the Netherlands.

The right-hander won the 2023 and 2015 50-over World Cups with Australia, while he also hit the winning runs as his nation claimed the T20 World Cup title in 2021.

Across 286 international matches (149 ODIs, 130 T20Is and seven Tests), Maxwell scored over 7,000 runs and took 136 wickets.

articles.title: England should recall Jack Leach for South Africa Tests and stop leaving  spinners 'isolated', says Simon Harmer
articles.summary: South Africa's Simon Harmer tells Sky Sports Cricket Podcast that fellow spinner Jack Leach would give England "control" when they face the Proteas live on Sky Sports this winter; Leach has not played for his country for two years; Harmer feels more spin-bowling coaches needed in England
articles.body:
Since Ben Stokes' international retirement in June, England have rejigged the balance of their side with Dan Lawrence's part-time off-spin now supporting four fast bowlers - a policy they could maintain when they play South Africa in three Tests from December 17.

However, Proteas frontline off-spinner Harmer, a county-cricket stalwart with Essex, bagged 14 wickets in three games in the just-completed 2-1 series win at home to Australia, including a 10-wicket match haul in the deciding Test at Cape Town.

Somerset left-arm spinner Leach last played for England two years ago - he does not have a central contract - and national selector Marcus North recently told the Wisden Cricket Weekly podcast that the team were moving in a "different direction."

Harmer, though, told the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast Leach, who has 142 wickets in 39 Tests to date an an average of 34.07, "would be his guy" as England prepare to tackle South Africa in Johannesburg, Centurion and Cape Town, live on Sky Sports.

"If you are going to play a spinner at those venues, you need, in the first innings, somebody who can hold an end so that your seamers can rotate, attack and bowl four overs of aggressive, fast bowling.

"If you don't have that control, it makes it very difficult to find 90 overs in a day and how that stacks up with your seamers. So, for me, Leach is still the guy for England.

"I know Marcus North was on a podcast saying that they're moving away from him, but I just don't understand [that].

"I'm sure the chats are, 'well, he doesn't bowl teams out on day five', but the amount of control that he gives you, I just think at the venues that South Africa will be hosting England, if you are going to take a spinner, he is probably your guy."

'England need to be proactive improving spin bowling'

Harmer also namechecked Shoaib Bashir - who is on an England central contract - Yorkshire's Dom Bess and Sussex's Jack Carson as players good enough for international cricket, but says they need more guidance at domestic level.

England recently appointed former Glamorgan coach and ex-Yorkshire spinner Richard Dawson as elite national spin bowling lead in an attempt to boost that element of the game.

Harmer said: "I worked with [former Leicestershire spinner] Carl Crowe for the first time at the SA20 with Durban's Super Giants and he is an absolute genius when it comes to spin bowling. He understands the game and the biomechanics of spin bowling.

"How he isn't being utilised more within the county system, I don't understand.

"It's not a lack of resources, it's just a lack of want to get [spin] structures into the county game.

"I think as a result of that, a lot of spinners feel isolated, feel alone, like they don't have the means in order for them to take their game to the next level.

"I think it's something that needs to be looked at. How are guys being developed when they are not with the England national team?

"You've got [England assistant coach] Jeetan Patel working with the spinners there, but I haven't seen him working with spinners at a county game or coming to watch.

"What happens is that England will wait until they don't have any spinners and then they will start to try and problem solve instead of being proactive. There are plenty of good spinners in England but they just don't have the tools necessary to upskill."

Sky Sports Cricket pundit Michael Atherton said after listening to Harmer's comments about spin on the podcast: "I agree with him.

"When I was bowling leg-spin as a very young first-class cricketer, the absence of knowledge was a big thing, particularly around leg-spin.

"When I went on my first Ashes tour to Australia, I was taken speaking to people who know about leg-spin intimately for the first time, whereas in England it was all a bit of a mystery.

articles.summary: When will Hardik Pandya return to the Indian team? How is the all-rounder's fitness? When will he be seen wearing India colours again?
articles.body: When will Hardik Pandya return to the Indian team? How is the all-rounder's fitness? When will he be seen wearing India colours again?These were some of the questions put to India captain Shubman Gill during his press conference ahead of the first ODI against New Zealand in Auckland on Wednesday.Pandya's absence from international cricket has been a talking point, with fans waiting for an update on his return. The all-rounder last represented India in the 2026 T20 World Cup final in Ahmedabad. Since then, his only competitive appearances have come in the Indian Premier League for Mumbai Indians.Pandya has missed several international assignments since the T20 World Cup, including India's home series against Afghanistan and tours of Ireland and England. He was also unavailable for the home ODI series against the West Indies and is missing the ongoing tour of New Zealand.Gill said the team management has been in regular touch with Pandya and highlighted the importance of having a player of his ability in the side.He also revealed that the all-rounder suffered a niggle before the India A match."We have had multiple conversations, he is a quality player - not many in the world have what he can do. Hopefully he plays some domestic and gets back. Unfortunate he got a niggle before India A match," Gill told reporters ahead of the first ODI.Hardik's return to solve India's lower-order concernsGill also explained how Pandya's return would help India strengthen their lower order. The captain believes the all-rounder's presence would take care of the No. 7 and No. 8 batting positions."Whenever Hardik bhai comes back, no 7/8 will also be taken care of. Happy with batting group leading up to the ODI World Cup," he said.India will begin their five-match ODI series against New Zealand at Eden Park in Auckland on November 4. The second match will be played in Wellington on November 7, followed by the third ODI in Hamilton on November 10.The teams will then move to Mount Maunganui for the final two matches on November 13 and 15.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Back in ODIs, Finn Allen looks to adapt in middle-order
articles.summary: Finn Allen is ready to embrace a new challenge as New Zealand look to explore his potential in the middle-order ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup.
articles.body: Finn Allen is ready to embrace a new challenge as New Zealand look to explore his potential in the middle-order ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup. The explosive opener, who last played an ODI for the Black Caps in Bangladesh in 2023, has been added to the squad for the fourth and fifth matches of the ODI series against India.With New Zealand exploring options to strengthen their middle-order, Allen could be asked to take on opposition spinners and target the fifth or sixth bowler, adding another dimension to his aggressive batting.“It’s an exciting opportunity to try something different. It’s a role I haven’t explored much before, and I’m looking forward to the challenge. The idea is to have an impact against spin through the middle overs and, hopefully, be set to accelerate towards the end of the innings,” Allen said.He said the key would be to adjust his tempo to the demands of ODI cricket while retaining his attacking intent. With only two fielders allowed outside the circle during the powerplay, compared to four after it, he believes the changing field restrictions offer different opportunities to score and rotate strike.The 27-year-old, who has scored 582 runs in 22 ODIs at an average of 27.71, including five half-centuries, believes adapting his tempo rather than abandoning his natural attacking instincts will be crucial in the 50-over format.“Having the same intent and approach is important for me. It’s about choosing lower-risk options at times, hitting fours along the ground instead of going for sixes, and being diligent with running between the wickets. I want to rotate strike comfortably in the middle order, while still putting pressure on the bowlers,” he said.Allen acknowledged that batting in the middle-order would require him to assess match situations quickly, whether New Zealand are rebuilding after early wickets or looking to accelerate from a strong position.“When the team is struggling, you need to absorb pressure but also find ways to put it back on the opposition. If the team is doing well, you have to do the same, but in a slightly different way. It’s about reading the situation quickly,” he said.Having missed out on New Zealand’s plans during the 2023 ODI World Cup, Allen believes his experience across leagues and domestic cricket has helped him understand his game better. Appearances in one-day cricket for Auckland have also allowed him to work on adapting his approach.“Technically, I feel my game is in a good place. Having played more cricket, I can control my innings better and adapt to different conditions,” he said.With Kane Williamson’s retirement opening up opportunities in New Zealand’s top order, Allen said, “Thankfully, I don’t have to try and replace Kane. It’s pretty tough to live up to.”(Tune-In: Watch New Zealand vs India 1st ODI live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network Sony LIV on Nov 4, 2026)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'The Big Show' is over: Glenn Maxwell announces retirement from international cricket
articles.summary: Maxwell, popularly known as 'The Big Show', represented Australia in 149 ODIs, 130 T20Is and seven Test matches. He was part of Australia's 2015 and 2023 ODI...
articles.body:
Australian all-rounder Glenn Maxwell has announced his retirement from international cricket, bringing an end to a career in which he entertained fans with his aggressive batting and unusual shots. Maxwell made the announcement on Tuesday during an episode of The Final Word podcast. His decision also includes his retirement from domestic 50-over and four-day cricket for Victoria. Maxwell, popularly known as 'The Big Show', represented Australia in 149 ODIs, 130 T20Is and seven Test matches. He was part of Australia's 2015 and 2023 ODI World Cup-winning teams and also played a key role in the team's T20 World Cup triumph in 2021. "I'm going to be announcing my retirement from international cricket and domestic games for Victoria in the 50 over and the four-day stuff, red ball completely," the 38-year-old told The Final Word podcast in an episode released on Tuesday.

Maxwell said he wants to give more attention to his fitness and prepare his body for the remaining tournaments in his career. "It's probably a time where I probably need to spend a little bit more time investing in the body to make sure I can get through the remaining couple of tournaments I've got in my career." He scored 3,990 runs in ODIs and 2,897 runs in T20 internationals. His last appearance for Australia came against Oman at the T20 World Cup in Sri Lanka in February.

Maxwell also made a special mark in T20 cricket. Along with India's Rohit Sharma, he remains one of only two players to score five international centuries in the format. With his off-spin bowling, he also picked up 128 wickets for Australia in the two shorter formats.

Maxwell had retired from ODI cricket last year but was hoping to play one final international match at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG). However, that possibility ended when Australia announced its squad for the upcoming series against England on Monday. The selectors have focused on younger players in their short-format plans. Maxwell admitted that he had hoped to get a farewell match at his home ground but understood the team's decision. "There was, I suppose, a small hope or discussion that I might have been able to potentially get a send-off game at the MCG, but I can completely understand the direction they're going with this squad," he said.
